SIBAWAYH:(هذاباباشتقاقكالأسماءلمواضعبنات.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذاباباشتقاقكالأسماءلمواضعبنات.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذاباباشتقاقكالأسماءلمواضعبنات.claim: ميسرة is cited as a feminine form on the مفعلة pattern, alongside forms such as المأدبة and معذرة.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p31/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p31/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p31/r2.claim: Category one changes inflection or a stem vowel without changing written form or meaning: أطهر/أطهر, يجازي/يجازى, بالبخل, and ميسرة.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p31/r2.anchor: أولها: الاختلاف في إعراب الكلمة، أو في حركة بنائها بما لا يزيلها عن صورتها في الكتاب ولا يغير معناها

AKHFASH:v1p203#2/r1.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p203#2/r1.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p203#2/r1.claim: If the debtor being pursued is insolvent, the creditor must wait until the debtor has means to repay.
AKHFASH:v1p203#2/r1.anchor: يقول: "وان كان ممن تقاضون ذو عسرة فعليكم ان تنظروا الى الميسرة"

AKHFASH:v1p203#2/r2.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p203#2/r2.speaker: some
AKHFASH:v1p203#2/r2.claim: Some supply an unexpressed predicate for كان in فنظرة إلى ميسرة.
AKHFASH:v1p203#2/r2.anchor: وقال بعضهم {فنظرة} وان شئت لم تجعل ل"كان" خبرا مضمرا

AKHFASH:v1p203#2/r3.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p203#2/r3.speaker: some
AKHFASH:v1p203#2/r3.claim: Others treat كان like وقع, so it needs no hidden predicate.

AKHFASH:v1p203#2/r4.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p203#2/r4.speaker: some
AKHFASH:v1p203#2/r4.claim: A reading ميسره is rejected because the pattern مفعل is not used in Arabic; موسره is allowed as a form from أيسر.
AKHFASH:v1p203#2/r4.anchor: وقال بعضهم {ميسره} وليست بجائزة لانه ليس في الكلام "مفعل". ولو قرؤها {موسره} جاز

AKHFASH:v1p203#2/r5.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p203#2/r5.speaker: some
AKHFASH:v1p203#2/r5.claim: Some read فناظره إلى ميسرة, treating ناظره as an imperative from ناظر and the phrase as jussive.
AKHFASH:v1p203#2/r5.anchor: وقال بعضهم {فناظره الى ميسرة} و {ميسرة} فجعلها "فاعل" [81ء] من "ناظر" وجزمها للامر.

AKHFASH:v1p203#2/r6.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p203#2/r6.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p203#2/r6.claim: أن تصدقوا خير لكم means that charity or foregoing repayment is better; أن تصدقوا is a nominal subject and خير لكم its predicate.
AKHFASH:v1p203#2/r6.anchor: وقال {وأن تصدقوا خير لكم} يقول: "الصدقة خير لكم". جعل {أن تصدقوا} اسما مبتدأ وجعل {خير لكم} خبر المبتدأ.

QURTUBI-FULL:4:6/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6/r3.speaker: عطاء والزهري
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6/r3.claim: Ata, al-Zuhri, and Kufan jurists say a wife cannot seek separation for her husband's poverty and should await payment as a court debt; they cite the respite for an insolvent debtor and the encouragement to marry the poor.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6/r3.anchor:
هذا قول عطاء والزهري. وإليه ذهب الكوفيون متمسكين بقوله تعالى:
وإن كان ذو عسرة فنظرة إلى ميسرة

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p94/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p94/r1.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p94/r1.claim: Al-Kalbi reports that Banu Amr b. Umayr demanded their principal from Banu al-Mughira, who pleaded hardship and asked for time until the crop came in; they refused, and the verse was revealed.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p94/r1.anchor: قال الكلبي: قالت بنو عمرو بن عمير لبني المغيرة: هاتوا رؤوس أموالنا ولكن الربا ندعه لكم

BURSEVI:v1p357#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p357#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p357#2/r1.claim: A creditor whose debtor is insolvent or whose goods have stagnated must grant respite until the debtor reaches solvency; maysara means ease or means.
BURSEVI:v1p357#2/r1.anchor: فالحكم نظرة وهي من الإنظار والإمهال

BURSEVI:v1p357#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p357#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p357#2/r2.claim: ‘That you remit’ means either forgive the entire debt of an insolvent borrower or grant delay; this is better for creditors and earns more reward, so those who know its benefit will do it.
BURSEVI:v1p357#2/r2.anchor: وتصدقكم بإسقاط الدين كله عمن أعسر من الغرماء أو بالتأخير والإنظار

BURSEVI:v1p357#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p357#2/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
BURSEVI:v1p357#2/r3.claim: The Prophet says that for every day a creditor delays a Muslim’s due debt, the creditor receives the reward of a charitable act.
BURSEVI:v1p357#2/r3.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم "لا يحل دين رجل مسلم فيؤخره إلا كان له بكل يوم صدقة"

BURSEVI:v1p357#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p357#2/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
BURSEVI:v1p357#2/r4.claim: The Prophet says that whoever gives an insolvent debtor time or waives the debt will be saved by God from the distress of Judgment Day.
BURSEVI:v1p357#2/r4.anchor: وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم "من أنظر معسرا أو وضع له أنجاه الله من كرب يوم القيامة"

BURSEVI:v1p357#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p357#2/r5.speaker: أمامة الباهلي
BURSEVI:v1p357#2/r5.claim: In a dream, Umāma al-Bāhilī saw that a loan earns eighteenfold while charity earns tenfold; he was told charity may reach a rich person, whereas a borrower comes only when needy.
BURSEVI:v1p357#2/r5.anchor: روي أن أمامة الباهلي رضي الله عنه رأى في المنام على باب الجنة مكتوبا القرض بثمانية عشر أمثاله والصدقة بعشر أمثالها

BURSEVI:v1p357#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p357#2/r6.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
BURSEVI:v1p357#2/r6.claim: The Prophet names three deeds that let a believer enter through any gate of Paradise and choose houris: pardon a killer, recite al-Ikhlāṣ ten times after obligatory prayers, or lend to someone who asks; one deed suffices.
BURSEVI:v1p357#2/r6.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم "ثلاث من جاء بهن يوم القيامة مع إيمان دخل من أي : أبواب الجنة شاء

BURSEVI:v1p357#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p357#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p357#2/r7.claim: Borrowing is commended in three cases: lacking means for God’s cause, shrouding a poor person who died destitute, or marrying to preserve chastity; borrow in trust that God will open the means to repay.
BURSEVI:v1p357#2/r7.anchor: واعلم أن الاستدانة في أحوال ثلاث في ضعف قوته في سبيل الله وفي تكفين فقير مات عن قلة وفقر وفي نكاح يطلب به العفة

BURSEVI:v1p357#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p357#2/r8.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
BURSEVI:v1p357#2/r8.claim: The Prophet says that one who borrows intending repayment is assigned angels who guard and pray for him until he repays.
BURSEVI:v1p357#2/r8.anchor: قال صلى الله عليه وسلم "من أدان دينا وهو ينوي قضاءه وكل به ملائكة يحفظونه ويدعون له حتى يقضيه"

BURSEVI:v1p357#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p357#2/r9.speaker: جماعة السلف
BURSEVI:v1p357#2/r9.claim: Groups among the early Muslims borrowed even without need, relying on this report about angels assigned to borrowers who intend repayment.
BURSEVI:v1p357#2/r9.anchor: وكان جماعة السلف يستقرضون من غير حاجة لهذا الخبر

BURSEVI:v1p357#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p357#2/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p357#2/r10.claim: A debtor should hasten to repay as soon as able, even before the due date.
BURSEVI:v1p357#2/r10.anchor: ومهما قدر على قضاء الدين فليبادر إليه ولو قبل وقته

BURSEVI:v1p357#2/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p357#2/r11.speaker: جبريل عليه السلام
BURSEVI:v1p357#2/r11.claim: A report from the Prophet, transmitted from Gabriel, says martyrdom expiates everything except debt; the warning is repeated three times.
BURSEVI:v1p357#2/r11.anchor: وعن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن جبريل عليه السلام : "الشهادة تكفر كل شيء إلا الدين يا محمد" ثلاثا

ELMALILI:2:278-281#2/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:278-281#2/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:278-281#2/r9.claim: An insolvent debtor must be given time until able to pay; forgiving the debt is better and brings greater reward than waiting.
ELMALILI:2:278-281#2/r9.anchor: o hâlde hüküm bi’z-zarûre hâl-i yüsrüne intizardır. Ona verebilecek bir hâle gelinceye kadar mühlet verilmek lâzım gelir

ELMALILI:2:278-281#2/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:278-281#2/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:278-281#2/r10.claim: The rule extends by implication to all debts: an insolvent debtor should not be imprisoned, and helping poor debtors escape debt through aid or remission is a major good.
ELMALILI:2:278-281#2/r10.anchor: Bu âyetin hükmü bi’d-delâle bütün düyûnâta şâmildir. Bu da ahkâm-ı müdâyenâtta bir esastır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:280/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:280/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:280/r1.claim: Rights, receivables, duties, and obligations can be legal, religious, moral, or some combination of these.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:280/r1.anchor: Haklar, alacaklar, ödev ve yükümlülükler yalnızca hukukî olanlardan ibaret değildir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:280/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:280/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:280/r2.claim: The law grants repentant usurers the right to reclaim principal, while religious and moral excellence requires not pressuring distressed debtors and granting time until they can pay.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:280/r2.anchor: Ana parayı almak, faizciliğe tövbe edenlerin hakkıdır, bu hakkı onlara hukuk bahşetmektedir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:280/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:280/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:280/r3.claim: Those able to do so do better by forgiving debts owed by people in hardship for God's pleasure.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:280/r3.anchor: durumu müsait olanların, darlık içinde bulunan kimselerdeki alacaklarını bağışlamaları ve bunu Allah rızâsı için yapmaları (tasadduk) kendileri için daha hayırlıdır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:280/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:280/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:280/r4.claim: This virtue applies to every kind of receivable, not only the principal owed to creditors who have repented of usury.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:280/r4.anchor: Bu faziletli davranış yalnızca faizcilikten tövbe eden alacaklıların ana paraları için değil, her nevi alacak için geçerlidir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:280/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:280/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:280/r5.claim: Islam's moral value is to grant interest-free extensions, or forgive the debt, from mercy rather than adding interest as pre-Islamic Arabs and contemporary capitalists and bankers do.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:280/r5.anchor: yeni faiz ilâvesiyle vade tanımak yerine, Allah rızâsı için ve müminin mânevî yapısının ayrılmaz bir parçası olan merhamet gereği

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p414/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p414/r1.speaker: نافع
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p414/r1.claim: Nāfiʿ alone reads ميسرة with ḍamma on the sīn.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p414/r1.anchor: فقرأ نافع وحده: إلى ميسرة بضم السين

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p414/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p414/r2.speaker: الباقون
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p414/r2.claim: All other readers use fatḥa on the sīn, and all readers turn the tāʾ marbūṭa into tāʾ with tanwīn in connected reading.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p414/r2.anchor: وقرأ الباقون: ميسرة بفتح السين، وكلهم قلب الهاء تاء ونونها

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p414/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p414/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p414/r3.claim: Abū ʿAlī accepts both vocalizations because the patterns مفعلة and مفعلة occur, though the ḍamma examples are less common.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p414/r3.anchor: قال أبو علي: حجة من قرأ إلى ميسرة أن مفعلة قد جاء في كلامهم كثيرا

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p414/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p414/r4.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p414/r4.claim: The ḍamma pattern is attested too, with examples المسربة and المشرقة, but not as frequently.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p414/r4.anchor: وأما من قرأ إلى ميسرة بضم السين فلأن مفعلة قد جاء أيضا في كلامهم

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p414/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p414/r5.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p414/r5.claim: The fatḥa reading is preferable because that form is more common than the ḍamma form.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p414/r5.anchor: فالقراءة الأولى أولى لأن الكلمة بفتح العين منها أكثر من الضم

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p414/r6.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p414/r6.speaker: سيبويه
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p414/r6.claim: Sībawayh says nouns of place from verbs with either vowel converge on the lighter of the two because a singular مفعل pattern is unavailable.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p414/r6.anchor: قال سيبويه: وأما ما كان يفعل منه مضموما، فهو بمنزلة ما كان يفعل منه مفتوحا

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p414/r7.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p414/r7.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p414/r7.claim: Abū ʿAlī limits Sībawayh’s statement to singular forms because the place noun being discussed is singular.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p414/r7.anchor: قال أبو علي: كلامه هذا في الآحاد، ألا ترى أنه يقصد مكان الفعل

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p414/r8.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p414/r8.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p414/r8.claim: Poetic plurals معون and مكرم do not challenge Sībawayh because they derive from معونة and مكرمة and are plural, not singular.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p414/r8.anchor: وما جاء في الشعر من معون ومكرم جمع معونة ومكرمة لا يدخل على هذا لأنه جمع

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p414/r9.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p414/r9.speaker: أحمد بن موسى
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p414/r9.claim: Aḥmad ibn Mūsā explains that all readers mark the tāʾ and tanwīn in connected reading because singular forms without tāʾ do not occur.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p414/r9.anchor: قال أحمد بن موسى: وكلهم قلب الهاء تاء ونونها، يعني: في الوصل، يريد أنه: لم يقرأ أحد منهم إلى ميسرة

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p414/r10.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p414/r10.speaker: جميل
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p414/r10.claim: Jamīl’s verse uses معون, a rare plural of معونة, illustrating that such forms can occur in poetry.

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p414/r11.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p414/r11.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p414/r11.claim: A second transmitted verse uses مألكا, a plural of مألكة meaning رسالة.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p414/r11.anchor: وروي: أبلغ النعمان عني مألكا ... إنه قد طال حبسي وانتظاري

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p414/r12.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p414/r12.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p414/r12.claim: Sībawayh may dismiss one or two rare forms and say a pattern does not exist because he does not treat isolated exceptions as a productive class.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p414/r12.anchor: فربما أطلق القول، فقال: ليس في الكلام كذا، وإن كان قد جاء عليه حرف أو حرفان

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p143/r1.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p143/r1.speaker: نافع في جماعة من الصحابة
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p143/r1.claim: Nāfiʿ and a group of Companions read فنظرة إلى ميسرة.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p143/r1.anchor: ويشهد لهذا قراءة من قرأ: "فنظرة إلى ميسرة"، قرأ بها نافع في جماعة من الصحابة

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p143/r2.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p143/r2.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p143/r2.claim: The form ميسره is unusual because nouns on this pattern ordinarily take feminine tāʾ; it is best explained by elision of tāʾ, with the possessive suffix helping replace it, as in the Kufa explanation of إقام الصلاة.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p143/r2.anchor: وأما "إلى ميسره" فغريب؛ وذلك أنه ليس في الأسماء شيء على مفعل بغير تاء؛ لكنه بالهاء

QIRAAT-ER:2:280:5#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:2:280:5#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:2:280:5#1/r1.claim: The ʿusura reading changes internal vowels but retains the abstract sense of hardship.
QIRAAT-ER:2:280:5#1/r1.anchor: Canonical vowel variant changes internal voweling but preserves the abstract hardship meaning

QIRAAT-ER:2:280:9#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:2:280:9#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:2:280:9#1/r1.claim: Maysuratin is a canonical vowel variant without a major semantic shift.
QIRAAT-ER:2:280:9#1/r1.anchor: Canonical vowel variant maysuratin (maysuratin), with no major semantic shift

QIRAAT-ER:2:280:12#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:2:280:12#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:2:280:12#1/r1.claim: The form V tāʾ assimilates into ṣād, a phonetic compression with no change in meaning.
QIRAAT-ER:2:280:12#1/r1.anchor: Canonical assimilation of Form V tāʾ into ṣād, phonetic compression without semantic change

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p111#3/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p111#3/r1.speaker: شريح
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p111#3/r1.claim: Shurayh says the respite rule applied to usury, which had existed among the Ansar, rather than this debt; he cites the command to return trusts and judge justly.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p111#3/r1.anchor: فقال شريح هذه كانت في الربا وإنما كان الربا في الأنصار وإن الله تعالى يقول

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p111#3/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p111#3/r2.speaker: شريح
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p111#3/r2.claim: Shurayh says God would not command something only for people to disobey, and orders the debtor held beside the pillar until he pays.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p111#3/r2.anchor: فقال شريح هذه كانت في الربا وإنما كان الربا في الأنصار وإن الله تعالى يقول

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p111#3/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p111#3/r3.speaker: إبراهيم
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p111#3/r3.claim: Ibrahim takes the better charity to mean waiving the principal amount.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p111#3/r3.anchor: قال نا الثوري عن مغيرة عن إبراهيم في قوله تعالى ﴿ وأن تصدقوا خير لكم إن كنتم تعلمون ﴾ قال برأس المال

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p716/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p716/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p716/r10.claim: Banu al-Mughira complained of hardship and asked their creditors to wait until the harvest arrived, but the creditors refused; the verse was then revealed.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p716/r10.anchor: شكا بنو المغيرة العسرة وقالوا: أخرونا إلى أن تدرك الغلات، فأبوا أن يؤخروا، فنزلت

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p716/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p716/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p716/r11.claim: Some say this verse abrogated the pre-Islamic practice of selling an insolvent debtor; others say the practice had been ordered early in Islam, in which case the verse abrogated it, but absent that premise there is no abrogation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p716/r11.anchor: قيل: هذه الآية ناسخة لما كان في الجاهلية من بيع من أعسر بدين، وقيل: أمر به في صدر الإسلام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p716/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p716/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p716/r12.claim: عسرة means lack of money and tight circumstances, نظرة means postponement, and ميسرة means ease.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p716/r12.anchor: والعسرة ضيق الحال من جهة عدم المال، ومنه: جيش العسرة، والنظرة: التأخير، والميسرة: اليسر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p716/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p716/r13.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p716/r13.claim: The majority treats كان as complete in ذو عسرة, meaning that one of your debtors is insolvent; this is also Sibawayh's and Abu Ali's view.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p716/r13.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: ذو عسرة، على أن: كان، تامة، وهو قول سيبويه، وأبي علي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p716/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p716/r14.speaker: بعض الكوفيين
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p716/r14.claim: Some Kufans allow كان to be incomplete here.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p716/r14.anchor: وأجاز بعض الكوفيين أن تكون: كان، ناقصة هنا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p716/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p716/r15.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p716/r15.claim: One proposed ellipsis supplies من غرمائكم as the predicate, and another supplies a creditor's right against the debtor; the grammarians reject deleting كان's predicate either by omission or ellipsis.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p716/r15.anchor: وقدّر الخبر: وإن كان من غرمائكم ذو عسرة فحذف المجرور الذي هو الخبر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p716/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p716/r16.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p716/r16.claim: The grammarians do not permit deleting the predicate of كان, whether by simple omission or ellipsis.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p716/r16.anchor: وحذف خبر كان لا يجوز عند أصحابنا، لا اقتصارا ولا اختصارا لعلة ذكروها في النحو

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p716#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p716#2/r1.speaker: أبي وابن مسعود وعثمان وابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p716#2/r1.claim: Ubayy, Ibn Masud, Uthman, and Ibn Abbas read ذا عسرة in the accusative; al-A'mash reads معسرا.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p716#2/r1.anchor: وقرأ أبي، وابن مسعود، وعثمان، وابن عباس: ذا عسرة. وقرأ الأعمش: معسرا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p716#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p716#2/r2.speaker: الداني عن أحمد بن موسى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p716#2/r2.claim: Al-Dani transmits from Ahmad ibn Musa that a codex reading has كان with an implicit pronoun subject referring to the debtor, understood from the preceding context.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p716#2/r2.anchor: وحكى الداني عن أحمد بن موسى أنها كذلك في مصحف أبي علي إن في كان اسمها ضميرا تقديره: هو، أي: الغريم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p716#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p716#2/r3.speaker: أبان بن عثمان
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p716#2/r3.claim: Aban ibn Uthman reads ومن كان ذا عسرة; al-Mahdawi also reports فإن كان with fa in Uthman's codex.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p716#2/r3.anchor: وقرىء: ومن كان ذا عسرة، وهي قراءة أبان بن عثمان. وحكى المهدوي أن في مصحف عثمان: فإن كان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p716#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p716#2/r4.speaker: بعضهم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p716#2/r4.claim: Some say the accusative ذا and the reading معسرا apply specifically to usury debts, while nominative readings extend to all debts; the author says that distinction is not required because the passage and revelation concern usury.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p716#2/r4.anchor: فمن نصب ذا عسرة أو قرأ معسرا، وذلك بعد: إن كان، فقيل: يختص بأهل الربا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p716#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p716#2/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p716#2/r5.claim: The verse's apparent sense presents solvency as the default and insolvency as an exceptional state that must be established.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p716#2/r5.anchor: وقيل: ظاهر الآية يدل على أن الأصل الإيسار، وأن العدم طارئ جاذب يحتاج إلى أن يثبت

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p716#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p716#2/r6.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p716#2/r6.claim: The majority reads فنظرة with a kasra-like vowel on ظ; Abu Raja, Mujahid, al-Hasan, al-Dahhak, and Qatada read it with ظ still, a Tamimi dialect like كبد for كبد.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p716#2/r6.anchor: وقرأ أبو رجاء، ومجاهد، والحسن، والضحاك، وقتادة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p716#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p716#2/r7.speaker: عطاء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p716#2/r7.claim: Ata reads فناظرة; al-Zajjaj parses it as a verbal noun, supported by Qur'anic forms such as كاذبة, فاقرة, and خائنة.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p716#2/r7.anchor: وقرأ عطاء: فناظرة، على وزن: فاعلة وخرجه الزجاج على أنها مصدر كقوله تعالى: ليس لوقعتها كاذبة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p716#2/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p716#2/r8.speaker: عطاء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p716#2/r8.claim: Ata's فناظرة can mean the creditor waits for the debtor or is the holder of a respite, by an attributive noun formation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p716#2/r8.anchor: قرأ عطاء: فناظرة، بمعنى: فصاحب الحق ناظره، أي: منتظره، أو: صاحب نظرته

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p716#2/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p716#2/r9.speaker: عطاء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p716#2/r9.claim: Ata also reads فناظره as an imperative to grant the debtor a respite and treat him leniently.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p716#2/r9.anchor: وعنه: فناظره، على الأمر بمعنى: فسامحه بالنظرة، وباشره بها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p716#2/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p716#2/r10.speaker: مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p716#2/r10.claim: Mujahid makes the form an imperative, with its pronoun referring to the debtor; Abdullah reads فناظروه, meaning that the creditors should wait for him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p716#2/r10.anchor: وعن مجاهد: جعلاه أمرا، والهاء ضمير الغريم. وقرأ عبد الله: فناظروه، أي: فأنتم ناظروه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p716#2/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p716#2/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p716#2/r11.claim: On the six readings treated as nouns of action or infinitives, an omitted subject is understood: the creditor's duty is to wait for payment until the debtor has means.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p716#2/r11.anchor: فهذه ست قراءات، ومن جعله اسم مصدر أو مصدرا فهو يرتفع على أنه خبر مبتدأ محذوف تقديره

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p716#2/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p716#2/r12.speaker: نافع
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p716#2/r12.claim: Nafi alone reads ميسرة with a damma on sin, a less common Hijazi dialect; the majority reads the more common fatha used in Najd.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p716#2/r12.anchor: وقرأ نافع وحده: ميسرة، بضم السين، والضم لغة أهل الحجاز، وهو قليل كمقبرة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p716#2/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p716#2/r13.speaker: عبد الله
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p716#2/r13.claim: Abdullah reads ميسوره with a suffix referring to the debtor; al-Akhfash treats it as a verbal noun like معقول and مجلود.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p716#2/r13.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله: إلى ميسوره، على وزن مفعول مضافا إلى ضمير الغريم، وهو عند الأخفش مصدر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p718/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p718/r1.speaker: الأخفش
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p718/r1.claim: Al-Akhfash analyzes ميسوره as a verbal noun, like معقول and مجلود, meaning the acts of being discerning and enduring.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p718/r1.anchor: ولا مجلود، أي: عقل وجلد، ولم يثبت سيبويه مفعولا مصدرا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p718/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p718/r2.speaker: سيبويه
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p718/r2.claim: Sibawayh does not attest مفعولا as a verbal noun, whereas Ata and Mujahid read ميسره with the debtor's pronoun suffix, with either vowel on sin.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p718/r2.anchor: ولم يثبت سيبويه مفعولا مصدرا، وقرأ عطاء ومجاهد: إلى ميسره، بضم السين وكسر الراء بعدها ضمير الغريم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p718/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p718/r3.speaker: الفراء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p718/r3.claim: The fatha form with the suffix is explained by deleting the feminine tā before possessive suffixation, as in the cited poetry; al-Farra and later grammarians hold this analysis.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p718/r3.anchor: وخرج ذلك على حذف التاء لأجل الإضافة. كقوله: وأخلفوك عد الأمر الذي وعدوا أي: عدة، وهذا أعني حذف التاء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p718/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p718/r4.speaker: أبو علي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p718/r4.claim: Abu Ali explains the deleted-tā reading as motivated by the absence of singular nouns on the مَفْعَل pattern and adduces مألك, معون, and مكرم forms in poetry.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p718/r4.anchor: وأداهم إلى هذا التأويل: أن مفعلا ليس في الأسماء المفردة، فأما في الجمع فقد ذكروا ذلك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p718/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p718/r5.speaker: جميل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p718/r5.claim: Jamil's line has معون as evidence for the form, interpreted as the plural of معونة.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p718/r5.anchor: وفي قول جميل: بثين الزمي لا إن لا إن لزمته ... على كثرة الواشين أي معون

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p718/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p718/r6.speaker: أبو الفتح
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p718/r6.claim: Abu al-Fath instead treats the form as a singular with its tā deleted.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p718/r6.anchor: وتأول أبو الفتح على أنها مفردة حذف منها التاء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p718/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p718/r7.speaker: سيبويه
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p718/r7.claim: Sibawayh is reported to deny مَفْعَل among singular forms, though مهلك is transmitted with three vowels; al-Kisai allows a singular مَفْعَل without contradicting Sibawayh because rare forms are not counted.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p718/r7.anchor: وقال سيبويه: ليس في الكلام مفعل، يعني في الآحاد، كذا قال أبو علي، وحكي عن سيبويه: مهلك، مثلث اللام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p718/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p718/r8.speaker: ابن عباس وشريح
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p718/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas and Shurayh say the creditor's obligation to defer payment applies specifically to usury debts.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p718/r8.anchor: أهذا الإنظار يختص بدين الربا؟ وهو قول ابن عباس، وشريح

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p718/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p718/r9.speaker: أبو هريرة والحسن وعطاء والضحاك والربيع بن خثيم وعامة الفقهاء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p718/r9.claim: Abu Hurayra, al-Hasan, Ata, al-Dahhak, al-Rabi ibn Khuthaym, and most jurists say the rule covers every insolvent debtor, whether or not the debt arose from usury.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p718/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p718/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p718/r10.claim: The source cites a hadith promising that whoever defers payment for an insolvent person and remits the debt will be shaded by God on the day with no other shade.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p718/r10.anchor: منها: «من أنظر معسرا، ووضع عنه، أظله الله في ظله يوم لا ظل إلا ظله»

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p718/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p718/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p718/r11.claim: A further report describes a servant who says he did no good except use his wealth to ease the poor and defer insolvent debtors; God says He has greater right to pardon the servant.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p718/r11.anchor: وأنظر المعسر، فيقول الله عز وجل: أنا أحق بذلك منك. فتجاوزوا عن عبدي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p718/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p718/r12.speaker: الضحاك والسدي وابن زيد والجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p718/r12.claim: Al-Dahhak, al-Suddi, Ibn Zayd, and the majority say voluntary charity means remitting all or part of the debtor's principal, which is better than merely deferring payment.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p718/r12.anchor: أي: تصدقوا على الغريم برأس المال أو ببعضه خير من الإنظار، قاله الضحاك والسدي، وابن زيد، والجمهور

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p718/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p718/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p718/r13.claim: The alternative that charity means simply waiting rather than demanding payment is weak: deferral is already obligatory, and the comparative خير should retain its usual comparative sense, introducing a new benefit.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p718/r13.anchor: وهذا ضعيف، لأن الإنظار للمعسر واجب على رب الدين، فالحمل على فائدة جديدة أولى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p719/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p719/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p719/r1.claim: The good in giving charity is beautiful praise in this world and a great reward in the next.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p719/r1.anchor: حصول الثناء الجميل في الدنيا والأجر الجزيل في الآخرة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p719/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p719/r2.speaker: قتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p719/r2.claim: Qatada says creditors are encouraged to remit principal for debtors, whether rich or poor.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p719/r2.anchor: وقال قتادة: ندبوا إلى أن يتصدقوا برؤوس أموالهم على الغني والفقير

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p719/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p719/r3.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p719/r3.claim: The majority assimilates the تاء of تصدقوا into صاد; Asim deletes the تاء, while Abdullah's codex preserves the original two تاءs. Assimilation and deletion are successive forms of easing pronunciation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p719/r3.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: وأن تصدقوا، بإدغام التاء في الصاد، وقرأ عاصم: تصدقوا، بحذف التاء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p719/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p719/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p719/r4.claim: In إن كنتم تعلمون, knowing is meant to entail acting; alternatively it means knowing charity is better than respite and collection, or that God's command is best for people.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p719/r4.anchor: إن كنتم تعلمون: يريد العمل، فجعله من لوازم العلم، وقيل: تعلمون فضل التصدق على الإنظار والقبض

QUSHAYRI:v1p127/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p127/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p127/r1.claim: Whoever heeds admonition, restrains desire, and stops persisting is granted respite in the present.
QUSHAYRI:v1p127/r1.anchor: ومن انتبه بزواجر الوعظ ، وكبح لجام الهوى ، ولم يطلق عنان الإصرار فله الإمهال في الحال

QUSHAYRI:v1p127/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p127/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p127/r2.claim: If he returns to those blameworthy states, he should expect near eradication and sudden punishment.
QUSHAYRI:v1p127/r2.anchor: فإن عاد إلى مذموم تلك الأحوال فلينتظروا أوشك الاستئصال وفجاءة النكال

QUSHAYRI:v1p127/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p127/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p127/r3.claim: Actions undertaken by God's leave are accompanied by good and blessing.
QUSHAYRI:v1p127/r3.anchor: ما كان بإذن منه - سبحانه - من التصرفات فمقرون بالخيرات ، ومصحوب بالبركات

QUSHAYRI:v1p127/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p127/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p127/r4.claim: Actions that follow caprice invite erasure, and their outcome is loss.
QUSHAYRI:v1p127/r4.anchor: وما كان بمتابعة الهوى يسلط عليه المحق ، وكانت عاقبة أمره الخسران

QUSHAYRI:v1p127/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p127/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p127/r5.claim: A Muslim is better served by relying on what the Lord promises than attaching the heart to what the self wants.
QUSHAYRI:v1p127/r5.anchor: الاكتفاء بموعود الرب خير للمسلم من تعليق قلبه بمقصود نفسه

QUSHAYRI:v1p127/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p127/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p127/r6.claim: The self's desired object comes from its suggestions, whereas the divine promise comes from what the Real has guaranteed.
QUSHAYRI:v1p127/r6.anchor: مقصودك من تسويلات النفس ، وموعودك مما ضمنه الحق

QUSHAYRI:v1p127/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p127/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p127/r7.claim: One who persists in wrongdoing has no weight, value, or standing with God.
QUSHAYRI:v1p127/r7.anchor: إن صاحب الإصرار ليس له عندنا وزن ولا مقدار ، ولا قدر ولا أخطار

QUSHAYRI:v1p127/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p127/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p127/r8.claim: Once a judge establishes that an imprisoned debtor is insolvent, the judge may not continue imprisoning him.
QUSHAYRI:v1p127/r8.anchor: إذا تقرر عند القاضي إفلاس المحبوس فلا تحل له استدامة حبسه

QUSHAYRI:v1p127/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p127/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p127/r9.claim: The creditor's established claim remains the debtor's obligation, but the insolvent debtor is granted delay and respite.
QUSHAYRI:v1p127/r9.anchor: وإن ظهرت لذي الحق حجة المفلس فذلك مرتهن بحق خصمه ، ولكنه في إمهال وإنظار

QUSHAYRI:v1p127/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p127/r10.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p127/r10.claim: God treats human beings with mercy despite knowing their insolvency, incapacity, sincere need, and exclusive turning to Him.
QUSHAYRI:v1p127/r10.anchor: فمع علمه بإعسارنا وعجزنا ، وصدق افتقارنا إليه وانقطاعنا له - يرحمنا

QUSHAYRI:v1p127/r11.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p127/r11.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p127/r11.claim: The insolvent debtor has no income from assets or commercial capital; an indebtedness allotment is the only financial avenue, while one destitute in livelihood depends solely on his Master.
QUSHAYRI:v1p127/r11.anchor: ليس للفقير المفلس وجه يحصل له منه شيء إلا من حيث ما جعل الله سبحانه من سهم الغارمين

QUSHAYRI:v1p127/r12.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p127/r12.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p127/r12.claim: Return is bodily and personal at resurrection, and inward through the heart's accounting in every breath.
QUSHAYRI:v1p127/r12.anchor: الرجوع على ضربين : بالأبشار والنفوس غدا عند التوفي ، وبالأسرار والقلوب في كل نفس محاسبة

QUSHAYRI:v1p127/r13.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p127/r13.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p127/r13.claim: The present accounting and demand are more pressing than the promised reckoning that will occur at resurrection.
QUSHAYRI:v1p127/r13.anchor: فنقد مطالبته أحق مما سيكون في القيامة من وعده

ALUSI-FULL:v3p53#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p53#2/r1.speaker: أبو المسعود
ALUSI-FULL:v3p53#2/r1.claim: Abu al-Masʿud and others infer that an able debtor who refuses payment is an oppressor subject to imprisonment and other penalties.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p53#2/r1.anchor: قال المولى أبو المسعود وغيره : وإستدل بالآية على أن الممتنع عن أداء الدين مع القدرة ظالم يعاقب بالحبس وغيره

ALUSI-FULL:v3p53#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p53#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p53#2/r2.claim: The complete-verb reading of kāna means that the debtor falls into hardship because of lacking money; some Kufans instead treat it as incomplete, with an omitted predicate describing the creditor relationship.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p53#2/r2.anchor: على إن كان تامة وجوز بعض الكوفيين إن تكون ناقصة و ( ذو ) اسمها والخبر محذوف

ALUSI-FULL:v3p53#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p53#2/r3.speaker: عثمان
ALUSI-FULL:v3p53#2/r3.claim: ʿUthman reads the phrase with the accusative dhā ʿusra, while another reading adds man kāna dhā ʿusra; both make kāna incomplete with an implicit debtor subject.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p53#2/r3.anchor: وقرأ عثمان رضي الله تعالى عنه ذا عسرة وقرئ ومن كان ذا عسرة وعلى القراءتين ( كان ) ناقصة

ALUSI-FULL:v3p53#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p53#2/r4.speaker: الكلبي
ALUSI-FULL:v3p53#2/r4.claim: Al-Kalbi gives the occasion: Banu al-Mughira asked Banu ʿAmr ibn ʿUmayr to delay their debt until the crop ripened, but they refused.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p53#2/r4.anchor: والآية نزلت كما قال الكلبى : حين قالت بنو المغيرة لبنى عمرو ابن عمير : نحن اليوم أهل عسرة فأخرونا إلى أن تدرك الثمرة فأبوا

ALUSI-FULL:v3p53#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p53#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p53#2/r5.claim: The conditional particle makes naẓira its answer; the word may be a subject with an omitted predicate, a subject governed by an omitted verb, or a predicate after an omitted noun such as the obligation.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p53#2/r5.anchor: الفاء جواب الشرط ونظرة مبتدأ خبره محذوف أي فعليكم نظرة أو فاعل بفعل مضمر

ALUSI-FULL:v3p53#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p53#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p53#2/r6.claim: Naẓira means waiting, here the creditor's granting time and postponing collection.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p53#2/r6.anchor: والنظرة كالنظرة بسكون الظاء الإنتظار والمراد به الإمهال والتأخير

ALUSI-FULL:v3p53#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p53#2/r7.speaker: عطاء
ALUSI-FULL:v3p53#2/r7.claim: ʿAta reads fanāẓirahu as a noun with the debtor as the one awaited and given respite.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p53#2/r7.anchor: وقرأ عطاء فناظره بإضافة ناظر إلى ضمير ( ذو عسرة ) أي فالمستحق ناظره أي منتظره وممهله

ALUSI-FULL:v3p53#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p53#2/r8.speaker: عطاء
ALUSI-FULL:v3p53#2/r8.claim: ʿAta also reads fanāẓirahu as a reciprocal imperative meaning to deal leniently by granting time.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p53#2/r8.anchor: وعنه أيضا فناظره أمرا من المفاعلة أي فسامحه بالنظرة

ALUSI-FULL:v3p53#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p53#2/r9.speaker: حمزة ونافع
ALUSI-FULL:v3p53#2/r9.claim: Hamza and Nafiʿ read maysura with a damma on the sin; the form has dialectal parallels, and readings with deleted feminine tāʾ are explained as construct forms.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p53#2/r9.anchor: وقرأ حمزة ونافع ميسرة بضم السين وهما لغتان كمشرقه ومشرقه وقرئ بهما مضافين بحذف التاء وإقامة الإضافة مقامها

ALUSI-FULL:v3p53#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p53#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p53#2/r10.claim: Alusi answers the objection that the damma form of mafʿal is absent or rare by analyzing the word as mafʿala, or as a plural like makrama; another analysis derives it from maysur with the wāw elided and indicated by the damma.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p53#2/r10.anchor: فاندفع ما أورد على هذه القراءة بأن مفعلا بالضم معدوم أو شاذ وحاصله أنها مفعلة لا مفعل

ALUSI-FULL:v3p53#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p53#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p53#2/r11.claim: The phrase an taṣaddaqu has one of its two tāʾs omitted; a variant doubles ṣād by assimilating the second tāʾ.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p53#2/r11.anchor: بحذف إحدى التاءين وقرئ بتشديد الصاد على أن أصله تتصدقوا فقلبت التاء الثانية صادا وأدغمت

ALUSI-FULL:v3p53#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p53#2/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p53#2/r12.claim: Charity here means forgiving all or part of the principal owed by insolvent debtors.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p53#2/r12.anchor: أي وتصدقكم على معسرى غرمائكم برءوس أموالكم كلا أو بعضا

ALUSI-FULL:v3p53#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p53#2/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p53#2/r13.claim: The preference for charity over delay means it brings greater reward, or is better than collected money because collection passes while charity's reward remains.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p53#2/r13.anchor: أي أكثر ثوابا من الإنظار أو خير مما تأخذونه لنفاذ ذلك وبقاء هذا

ALUSI-FULL:v3p53#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p53#2/r14.speaker: الضحاك
ALUSI-FULL:v3p53#2/r14.claim: Al-Dahhak says that granting respite is obligatory, while God describes charity as better than respite.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p53#2/r14.anchor: أخرج ابن المنذر عن الضحاك قال : النظرة واجبة وخير الله تعالى الصدقة على النظرة

ALUSI-FULL:v3p53#2/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p53#2/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p53#2/r15.claim: Alusi rejects the view that charity means merely postponement and weakens the report from ʿImran ibn Husayn that a creditor earns charity for each day of delay: delay is already obligatory, and خير لكم suits a recommendation rather than an obligation.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p53#2/r15.anchor: وضعفه الإمام مع مخالفته للمأثور بأن وجوب الإنظار ثبت بالآية الأولى فلا بد من حمل هذه الآية على فائدة زائدة

ALUSI-FULL:v3p53#2/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p53#2/r16.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن والضحاك وأئمة أهل البيت
ALUSI-FULL:v3p53#2/r16.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas, al-Hasan, al-Dahhak, and the Imams of the Prophet's family infer from the unrestricted wording that every insolvent debtor must be granted time, whether or not the debt is usury.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p53#2/r16.anchor: واستدل بإطلاق الآية من قال بوجوب إنظار المعسر مطلقا سواء كان الدين دين ربا أم لا وهو الذي ذهب اليه ابن عباس دضى الله تعالى عنه والحسن والضحاك وأئمة اهل البيت

ALUSI-FULL:v3p53#2/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p53#2/r17.speaker: شريح وإبراهيم النخعي وابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v3p53#2/r17.claim: Shurayh, Ibrahim al-Nakhaʿi, and Ibn ʿAbbas in another report limit obligatory respite to usury debts and interpret the verse accordingly.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p53#2/r17.anchor: وذهب شريح وإبراهيم النخعي وابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما في رواية عنه إلى أنه لا يحب إلا في دين الربا خاصة وتأولوا الآية على ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v3p53#2/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p53#2/r18.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p53#2/r18.claim: The omitted answer to if you know is that those who know this is better will act on it; the conditional is an exhortation.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p53#2/r18.anchor: جواب ( إن ) محذوف أي إن كنتم تعلمون أنه خير لكم عملتموه وفيه تحريض على الفعل

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p345/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p345/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p345/r7.claim: After the warning, Banu Amr al-Thaqafi and other usury creditors accepted repentance and principal, but Banu al-Mughira refused to defer collection from them until harvest, prompting this verse.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p345/r7.anchor: فلما نزلت الآية قال بنو عمرو الثقفي ومن كان يعامل بالربا من غيرهم: بل نتوب إلى الله،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p345/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p345/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p345/r8.claim: In the construction with kāna, the indefinite noun is its subject while its predicate may be omitted; the example means, if a man is righteous, honor him.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p345/r8.anchor: يعني وإن كان الذي عليه الدين معسرا، رفع الكلام باسم كان ولم يأت لها بخير وذلك جائز في النكرة،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p345/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p345/r9.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p345/r9.claim: An alternative parses kāna as meaning 'occurred,' in which case it needs no predicate.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p345/r9.anchor: وقيل "كان" بمعنى وقع، وحينئذ لا يحتاج إلى خبر،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p345/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p345/r10.speaker: أبو جعفر
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p345/r10.claim: Abu Ja'far reads ʿusra with a damma on the sīn.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p345/r10.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر عسرة بضم السين

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p345/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p345/r11.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p345/r11.claim: The command to grant respite is phrased as a declaration, with an implied obligation: the creditor must grant a period of delay.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p345/r11.anchor: {فنظرة} أمر في صيغة الخبر تقديره فعليه نظرة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p345/r12.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p345/r12.speaker: نافع
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p345/r12.claim: Nafiʿ reads maysara with a damma on the sīn; the other readers use a fatḥa.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p345/r12.anchor: قرأ نافع ميسرة بضم السين وقرأ الآخرون بفتحها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p345/r13.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p345/r13.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p345/r13.claim: Mujahid reads maysara in an annexed form, meaning ease and abundance.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p345/r13.anchor: وقرأ مجاهد ميسرة بضم السين مضافا ومعناها اليسار والسعة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p345/r14.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p345/r14.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p345/r14.claim: The phrase 'that you give charity' means waiving the principal for the insolvent debtor, which is better for creditors.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p345/r14.anchor: {وأن تصدقوا} أي تتركوا رءوس أموالكم إلى المعسر {خير لكم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p345/r15.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p345/r15.speaker: عاصم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p345/r15.claim: Asim reads the ṣād in taṣṣaddaqu softened; the other readers pronounce it doubled.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p345/r15.anchor: قرأ عاصم تصدقوا بتخفيف الصاد والآخرون بتشديدها.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:279-280/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:279-280/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:279-280/r7.claim: The verse can mean that a debtor has fallen into hardship; an alternate reading makes the debtor “one who has hardship.”
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:279-280/r7.anchor: وإن وقع غريم ذو عسرة. وقرىء «ذا عسرة»

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:279-280/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:279-280/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:279-280/r8.claim: “Then deferment” can be a ruling, an obligation upon creditors, or a command that it be a deferment.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:279-280/r8.anchor: فالحكم نظرة، أو فعليكم نظرة، أو فليكن نظرة

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:279-280/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:279-280/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:279-280/r9.claim: A reading can say that the creditor is waiting for payment or is the one granting respite; another is an imperative to grant respite.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:279-280/r9.anchor: أي فالمستحق ناظره بمعنى منتظره، أو صاحب نظرته على طريق النسب

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:279-280/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:279-280/r10.speaker: نافع وحمزة
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:279-280/r10.claim: They read maysarah with a damma on the sīn; both vocalizations are Arabic variants.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:279-280/r10.anchor: وقرأ نافع وحمزة بضم السين، وهما لغتان

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:279-280/r11.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:279-280/r11.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:279-280/r11.claim: Both forms are also read in annexation with the tāʾ omitted, as in the cited wording from 9:77.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:279-280/r12.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:279-280/r12.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:279-280/r12.claim: Giving charity means writing off the debt; ʿAsim reads the ṣād with a light pronunciation.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:279-280/r12.anchor: { وأن تصدقوا } بالإبراء. وقرأ عاصم بتخفيف الصاد

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:279-280/r13.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:279-280/r13.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:279-280/r13.claim: Forgiving the debt is more rewarded than granting time, or better than the amount received because its reward is multiplied and lasting.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:279-280/r13.anchor: أكثر ثوابا من الإنظار، أو خير مما تأخذون لمضاعفة ثوابه ودوامه

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:279-280/r14.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:279-280/r14.speaker: النبي
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:279-280/r14.claim: The source cites a Prophetic report that a Muslim creditor who postpones a due debt receives charity for every day of delay.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:279-280/r14.anchor: لا يحل دين رجل مسلم فيؤخره إلا كان له بكل يوم صدقة

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:279-280#2/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:279-280#2/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:279-280#2/r1.claim: “If you know” refers to what this charitable conduct contains: a fine and abundant remembrance.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:279-280#2/r1.anchor: ما فيه من الذكر الجميل الجزيل

BIQAI-FULL:v1p541/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p541/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p541/r1.claim: The passage indicates that some will not abandon usury after it is prohibited, since they were not among those who believed.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p541/r1.anchor: أن طائقة منهم لا يذرونه بعد تحريمه بما أنهم ليسوا من الذين كانوا مؤمنين

BIQAI-FULL:v1p541/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p541/r2.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p541/r2.claim: War is forceful resistance over what one refuses to yield; here it conveys the severity of resisting the demand to give up usury.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p541/r2.anchor: قال الحرالي : والحرب مدافعة بشدة عن اتساع , المدافع بما يطلب منه الخروج عنه

BIQAI-FULL:v1p541/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p541/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p541/r3.claim: Mention of God and His Messenger magnifies the threat through God's grandeur and the Messenger's honor by association with Him.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p541/r3.anchor: ثم عظم أمرها بإيراد الاسم الأعظم فقال : { من الله } العظيم الجليل { ورسوله } صلى الله عليه وسلم

BIQAI-FULL:v1p541/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p541/r4.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p541/r4.claim: The Messenger was prepared for mercy, so the Prophet of mercy becomes an adversary to the usurer, severing the usurer's connection to the Merciful and intercessor.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p541/r4.anchor: وقال الحرالي : الذي هيأه للرحمة , فكان نبي الرحمة محاربا له , فانقطعت وصلته من الرحيم

BIQAI-FULL:v1p541/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p541/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p541/r5.claim: If debtors repent by stopping the remaining usury, the creditors retain their original principal, as in a sale.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p541/r5.anchor: ما أمركم الله به من ترك ما بقي منه { فلكم رؤوس أموالكم } أي كما هو حال البيع

BIQAI-FULL:v1p541/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p541/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p541/r6.claim: Neither side should be wronged: creditors must not take the usurious excess, and debtors must not reduce the principal or delay payment unjustly.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p541/r6.anchor: لا تظلمون } أي بأخذ شيء مما بقي من الربا { ولا تظلمون } بنقص من رأس المال

BIQAI-FULL:v1p541/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p541/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p541/r7.claim: A debtor in hardship who cannot presently pay must be granted deferment until ease if the creditors insist on recovering their money.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p541/r7.anchor: وإن كان } أي وجد من المدينين { ذو عسرة } لا يقدر على الأداء في هذا الوقت { فنظرة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p541/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p541/r8.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p541/r8.claim: A deferment is a delay whose completion is awaited.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p541/r8.anchor: قال الحرالي : وهو التأخير المرتقب نجازه { إلى ميسرة }

BIQAI-FULL:v1p541/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p541/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p541/r9.claim: Nāfiʿ and Ḥamza read maysarah with a ḍamma on sīn, signaling the fullest ease; others read it with fatḥa, signaling an intermediate ease, so waiting for the broadest ease is more virtuous.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p541/r9.anchor: وقرأ نافع وحمزة بضم السين ؛ قال الحرالي : إنباء عن استيلاء اليسر وهي أوسع النظرتين , والباقون بالفتح

BIQAI-FULL:v1p541/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p541/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p541/r10.claim: Forgiving the debt is better for creditors in this world through blessing and compensation and in the next through abundant reward.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p541/r10.anchor: وأن تصدقوا } أي وصدقتكم على المعسر بتركه له , ذلكم { خير } في الدنيا بما يبارك الله سبحانه وتعالى

BIQAI-FULL:v1p541/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p541/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p541/r11.claim: The conditional “if you know” challenges those who claim knowledge to recognize the truth and act; otherwise their refusal is crooked ignorance.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p541/r11.anchor: إن كنتم من ذوي العلم فأنتم تعرفون صحة ما دعوتكم إليه مما يقتضي الإدبار عنه أو الإقبال عليه

BIQAI-FULL:v1p541/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p541/r12.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p541/r12.claim: Whoever dedicates himself to knowledge sees that relinquishing the whole debt is better than taking a portion of the good due.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p541/r12.anchor: وقال الحرالي : فأعلم سبحانه وتعالى أن من وضع كيانه للعلم فكان ممن يدوم علمه ؟ تنبه لأن خير الترك

BIQAI-FULL:v1p541/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p541/r13.speaker: عائشة رضي الله تعالى عنها
BIQAI-FULL:v1p541/r13.claim: According to al-Bukhari, when the final verses, or in a variant the final verses of al-Baqara on usury, were revealed, the Prophet recited them to people in the mosque and then prohibited trade in wine.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p541/r13.anchor: وروى البخاري في التفسير عن عائشة رضي الله تعالى عنها قالت : ( لما أنزلت الآيات الأواخر

BIQAI-FULL:v1p541/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p541/r14.speaker: ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما
BIQAI-FULL:v1p541/r14.claim: Al-Bukhari transmits Ibn ʿAbbās's statement that the final verse revealed to the Prophet was the usury verse.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p541/r14.anchor: وله عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما قال : ( آخر آية نزلت على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم آية الربا )

BIQAI-FULL:v1p541/r15.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p541/r15.speaker: ابن شهاب
BIQAI-FULL:v1p541/r15.claim: Abū ʿUbayd transmits Ibn Shihāb's report that the last Qur'anic material entrusted at the Throne was the verses of usury and debt.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p541/r15.anchor: ولأبي عبيد عن ابن شهاب قال : آخر القرآن عهدا بالعرش آية الربا وآية الدين

DURR-FULL:v2p111#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p111#2/r1.speaker: البراء بن عازب وزيد بن أرقم
DURR-FULL:v2p111#2/r1.claim: The Prophet allowed currency exchange when hand-to-hand and forbade it when deferred.
DURR-FULL:v2p111#2/r1.anchor: عن أبي المنهال قال: سألت البراء بن عازب وزيد بن أرقم عن الصرف فقالا: كنا تاجرين على عهد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

DURR-FULL:v2p111#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p111#2/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v2p111#2/r2.claim: The Prophet forbade trading fresh dates for dried dates after confirming that fresh dates lose weight when dried.
DURR-FULL:v2p111#2/r2.anchor: عن سعد بن وقاص أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم سئل عن اشتراء الرطب بالتمر فقال: أينقص الرطب إذا يبس قالوا: نعم فنهى عن ذلك

DURR-FULL:v2p111#2/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p111#2/r3.speaker: أبو بكر الصديق
DURR-FULL:v2p111#2/r3.claim: The Prophet warned that exchanging gold or silver for its own kind at a surplus places both the demander and the one supplying extra in the Fire.
DURR-FULL:v2p111#2/r3.anchor: عن أبي بكر الصديق سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: الذهب بالذهب والفضة بالفضة مثلا بمثل الزائد والمستزيد في النار

DURR-FULL:v2p111#2/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p111#2/r4.speaker: أبو بكرة
DURR-FULL:v2p111#2/r4.claim: Abu Bakra reports that the Prophet forbade currency exchange two months before his death.
DURR-FULL:v2p111#2/r4.anchor: عن أبي بكرة أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم نهى عن الصرف قبل موته بشهرين

DURR-FULL:v2p111#2/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p111#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p111#2/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the verse about granting respite to an insolvent debtor was revealed concerning usury.
DURR-FULL:v2p111#2/r5.anchor: من طريق مجاهد عن ابن عباس في قوله {وإن كان ذو عسرة فنظرة إلى ميسرة} قال: نزلت في الربا

DURR-FULL:v2p111#2/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p111#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p111#2/r6.claim: The command to delay applies to an insolvent person in usury, not to a trust, which must be returned to its owners.
DURR-FULL:v2p111#2/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس {وإن كان ذو عسرة فنظرة} قال: إنما أمر في الربا أن ينظر المعسر وليست النظرة في الأمانة

DURR-FULL:v2p111#2/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p111#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p111#2/r7.claim: In the usury context, “and that you remit it” means forgiving the debt owed by an insolvent person.
DURR-FULL:v2p111#2/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس {وإن كان ذو عسرة فنظرة إلى ميسرة} هذا في شأن الربا {وأن تصدقوا} بها للمعسر فتتركوها له

DURR-FULL:v2p111#2/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p111#2/r8.speaker: شريح
DURR-FULL:v2p111#2/r8.claim: When urged not to imprison an insolvent debtor, Shurayh held that this verse concerns usury among an Ansar group; ordinary trusts must instead be delivered as 4:58 commands.
DURR-FULL:v2p111#2/r8.anchor: عن ابن سيرين أن رجلين اختصما إلى شريح في حق فقضى عليه شريح وأمر بحبسه فقال رجل عنده: إنه معسر

DURR-FULL:v2p111#2/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p111#2/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p111#2/r9.claim: The insolvent person in the verse is the debtor who is being pursued for payment.
DURR-FULL:v2p111#2/r9.anchor: من طريق علي عن ابن عباس {وإن كان ذو عسرة} يعني المطلوب

DURR-FULL:v2p113/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p113/r1.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v2p113/r1.claim: The debtor receives respite on the principal until becoming wealthy; remitting the principal to a poor debtor is charity, and al-Abbas did so.
DURR-FULL:v2p113/r1.anchor: عن السدي {وإن كان ذو عسرة فنظرة} برأس المال إلى ميسرة يقول: إلى غنى {وأن تصدقوا} برؤوس أموالكم على الفقير

DURR-FULL:v2p113/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p113/r2.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v2p113/r2.claim: The rule covers every debt owed by a Muslim: do not imprison or demand payment from a debtor known to be insolvent until God grants ease; forgiving principal is better than waiting, and God prefers charity.
DURR-FULL:v2p113/r2.anchor: عن الضحاك في الآية قال: من كان ذا عسرة فنظرة إلى ميسرة وكذلك كل دين على المسلم فلا يحل لمسلم له دين على أخيه

DURR-FULL:v2p113/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p113/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v2p113/r3.claim: Forgiving an insolvent person's debt brings greater reward; declining to forgive is not sinful, but imprisoning an insolvent is sinful, and a debtor able to pay who refuses is recorded as unjust.
DURR-FULL:v2p113/r3.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير {وأن تصدقوا خير لكم} يعني من تصدق بدين له على معدم فهو أعظم لأجره

DURR-FULL:v2p113/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p113/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v2p113/r4.claim: Whoever gives an insolvent debtor more time or remits the debt will be sheltered by God on the Day when there is no shade but His.
DURR-FULL:v2p113/r4.anchor: عن أبي اليسر أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: من أنظر معسرا أو وضع عنه أظله الله في ظله يوم لا ظل إلا ظله

DURR-FULL:v2p113/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p113/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v2p113/r5.claim: A wealthy man who eased payment for those able to pay and delayed the insolvent was forgiven when God said He was more entitled to show such generosity.
DURR-FULL:v2p113/r5.anchor: عن حذيفة أن رجلا أتى به الله عز وجل فقال: ماذا عملت في الدنيا فقال له الرجل: ما عملت مثقال ذرة من خير

DURR-FULL:v2p113/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p113/r6.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v2p113/r6.claim: A creditor who delays collecting a right receives charity for each day of delay.
DURR-FULL:v2p113/r6.anchor: عن عمران بن حصين قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من كان له على رجل حق فأخره كان له بكل يوم صدقة

DURR-FULL:v2p113/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p113/r7.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v2p113/r7.claim: To have supplications answered and distress removed, a person should relieve an insolvent debtor.
DURR-FULL:v2p113/r7.anchor: عن ابن عمر قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من أراد أن تستجاب دعوته وأن تكشف كربته فليفرج عن معسر

DURR-FULL:v2p113/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p113/r8.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v2p113/r8.claim: Whoever delays an insolvent debtor until he can pay will have God delay his punishment until the debtor repents.
DURR-FULL:v2p113/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من أنظر معسرا إلى ميسرته أنظره الله بذنبه إلى توبته

DURR-FULL:v2p115/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p115/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v2p115/r1.claim: A wealthy man with no other good deeds regularly told his servants to overlook insolvent debtors, and God said He was more entitled to that generosity and forgave him.
DURR-FULL:v2p115/r1.anchor: عن أبي مسعود البدري قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم حوسب رجل ممن كان قبلكم فلم يوجد له من الخير شيء

IBNABIHATIM:v2p552#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p552#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v2p552#2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses the person in hardship as the debtor.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p552#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس وان كان ذو عسرة يعني : المطلوب .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p552#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p552#2/r2.speaker: أبان بن عثمان وعمر بن عبد العزيز
IBNABIHATIM:v2p552#2/r2.claim: Abān ibn ʿUthmān and ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz say someone whose only property is a dwelling is insolvent; if he has no surplus, he should be deferred until God provides for him.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p552#2/r2.anchor: عن ابان بن عثمان ، وعمر بن عبد العزيز ، انهما قالا جميعا : من لم يكن له الا مسكن

IBNABIHATIM:v2p552#2/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p552#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v2p552#2/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the verse was revealed concerning usury. He also distinguishes usury debt from trusts, which must be returned; Shurayḥ, Ibrāhīm, and Ibn ʿUmayr likewise link it to usury.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p552#2/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس ، قوله : وان كان ذو عسرة فنظرة إلى ميسرة انما امر في الربا ، ان ينظر المعسر ، وليست النظرة في الامانة

IBNABIHATIM:v2p552#2/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p552#2/r4.speaker: السدى
IBNABIHATIM:v2p552#2/r4.claim: Al-Suddī says the debtor is deferred without any increase being added to the debt.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p552#2/r4.anchor: عن السدى ، قوله : وان كان ذو عسرة فنظرة إلى ميسرة قال : يؤخره ولا يزد عليه بشيء .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p552#2/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p552#2/r5.speaker: عطاء
IBNABIHATIM:v2p552#2/r5.claim: ʿAṭāʾ applies the postponement to both usury debts and other debts.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p552#2/r5.anchor: عن ابن جريج ، قال عطاء : فنظرة إلى ميسرة في الربا والدين .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p552#2/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p552#2/r6.speaker: أبان بن عثمان وعمر بن عبد العزيز
IBNABIHATIM:v2p552#2/r6.claim: Abān ibn ʿUthmān and ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz explain the respite as lasting until God grants the debtor provision.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p552#2/r6.anchor: عن ابان بن عثمان ، وعمر بن عبد العزيز انهما قالا في قوله : فنظرة إلى ميسرة قالا : فلينظره إلى ان يرزقه الله .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p552#2/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p552#2/r7.speaker: أبو جعفر
IBNABIHATIM:v2p552#2/r7.claim: Abū Jaʿfar gives death as one interpretation of “to an ease.”
IBNABIHATIM:v2p552#2/r7.anchor: عن اسرائيل ، عن جابر عن أبي جعفر : وان كان ذو عسرة فنظرة إلى ميسرة قال : الموت .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p553/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p553/r1.speaker: السدى
IBNABIHATIM:v2p553/r1.claim: Al-Suddī interprets “to an ease” as reaching wealth.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p553/r1.anchor: عن السدى إلى ميسرة يقول : إلى غنى .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p553/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p553/r2.speaker: إبراهيم
IBNABIHATIM:v2p553/r2.claim: Ibrāhīm says that remission means forgiving the principal; Qatāda, al-Suddī, al-Rabīʿ, and Muqātil are reported similarly.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p553/r2.anchor: قال سفيان ، عن مغيرة ، عن ابراهيموان تصدقوا خير لكم قال : براس المال .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p553/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p553/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v2p553/r3.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr says a creditor who forgives a debt owed by an insolvent person receives greater reward.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p553/r3.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير ، في قوله : وان تصدقوا خير لكم يعني : من تصدق بدين له على معدم

IBNABIHATIM:v2p553/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p553/r4.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v2p553/r4.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr says forgiving an insolvent debtor brings greater reward, accepting forgiveness is not sinful, imprisoning an insolvent debtor is sinful, and an able debtor who withholds payment is unjust.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p553/r4.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير ، في قول الله : وان تصدقوا خير لكم فهو اعظم لاجره ، ومن لم يتصدق عليه لم ياثم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p95#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p95#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p95#2/r1.claim: The conditional clause follows the return of principal sums: since contracts have been annulled, creditors might expect immediate repayment, and the verse adds the case of an insolvent debtor.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p95#2/r1.anchor: عطف على قوله : { فلكم رؤوس أموالكم } لأن ظاهر الجواب أنهم يسترجعونها معجلة ، إذ العقود قد فسخت

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p95#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p95#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p95#2/r2.claim: The coordinated clause is an understood possible case, and ذُو here means a debtor in hardship.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p95#2/r2.anchor: والمعطوف عليه حالة مقدرة مفهومة لأن الجزاء يدل على التسبب ، والأصل حصول المشروط عند الشرط . والمعنى وإن حصل ذو عسرة ، أي غريم معسر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p95#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p95#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p95#2/r3.claim: The verse shows that ذُو can be annexed to something that does not denote a noble quality.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p95#2/r3.anchor: وفي الآية حجة على أن ( ذو ) تضاف لغير ما يفيد شيئا شريفا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p95#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p95#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p95#2/r4.claim: Naẓira means waiting; Nāfiʿ reads maysara with a damma on sīn and the other readers with a fatha, as a noun for ease opposed to hardship.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p95#2/r4.anchor: والنظرة بكسر الظاء الانتظار . والميسرة بضم السين في قراءة نافع وبفتحها في قراءة الباقين اسم لليسر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p95#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p95#2/r5.speaker: أبو علي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p95#2/r5.claim: The word maysara follows the mifaʿla pattern, as in the listed examples; Abu Ali says the pattern with fatha is more common in Arabic.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p95#2/r5.anchor: وهي مفعلة كمشرقة ومشربة ومألكة ومقدرة ، قال أبو علي ومفعلة بالفتح أكثر في كلامهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p95#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p95#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p95#2/r6.claim: The phrase then defer is the conditional answer, with an omitted predicate understood as deferment for him.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p95#2/r6.anchor: وجملة فنظرة جواب الشرط ، والخبر محذوف ، أي فنظرة له

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p95#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p95#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p95#2/r7.claim: The request may be obligatory or recommended. If hardship means complete insolvency, postponement is obligatory and abolishes sale or enslavement of a debtor unable to pay.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p95#2/r7.anchor: فإن أريد بالعسرة العدم أي نفاد ماله كله فالطلب للوجوب ، والمقصود به إبطال حكم بيع المعسر واسترقاقه في الدين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p95#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p95#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p95#2/r8.claim: The author says debtor-sale or enslavement existed in pre-Islamic custom and ancient Egyptian law, Roman law enslaved debtors, the Torah may have had something similar, and a report of the practice in early Islam is unestablished.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p95#2/r8.anchor: وقد قيل : إن ذلك كان حكما في الجاهلية وهو حكم قديم في الأمم كان من حكم المصريين ، ففي القرآن الإشارة إلى ذلك بقوله تعالى : { ما كان ليأخذ أخاه في دين الملك }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p95#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p95#2/r9.speaker: مالك والجمهور
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p95#2/r9.claim: If hardship means financial strain and harm from immediate payment, some jurists require delay; Malik and the majority recommend it, since the creditor may collect by selling the debtor's assets and kindness is not mandatory.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p95#2/r9.anchor: ويحتمل الندب ، وهو قول مالك والجمهور ، فمن لم يشأ لم ينظره ولو ببيع جميع ماله لأن هذا حق يمكن استيفاؤه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p95#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p95#2/r10.speaker: متأخرو قرطبة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p95#2/r10.claim: Later judges in Cordoba nevertheless deferred payment at their discretion to prevent harm from an immediate sale of property needed to secure the debtor's livelihood.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p95#2/r10.anchor: غير أن المتأخرين بقرطبة كانوا لا يقضون عليه بتعجيل الدفع ، ويؤجلونه بالاجتهاد لئلا يدخل عليه مضرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p95#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p95#2/r11.speaker: الجمهور
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p95#2/r11.claim: Although the verse concerns usurious transaction debts, the majority extend it to all debts because once usury is annulled, principal becomes ordinary debt and the postponement rule applies generally.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p95#2/r11.anchor: ومورد الآية على ديون معاملات الربا ، لكن الجمهور عمموها في جميع المعاملات ولم يعتبروا خصوص السبب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p95#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p95#2/r12.speaker: شريح
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p95#2/r12.claim: Shurayh restricts the postponement rule to debts originally bearing usury, whose usurious increment has been annulled.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p95#2/r12.anchor: وخالف شريح فخص الآية بالديون التي كانت على ربا ثم أبطل رباها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p96/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p96/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p96/r1.claim: Forgiving an insolvent debtor's debt and relieving distress by restoring his means is better; God calls it charity because it relieves hardship and aids someone in need.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p96/r1.anchor: وقوله : { وأن تصدقوا خير لكم } أي أن إسقاط الدين عن المعسر والتنفيس عليه بإغنائه أفضل ، وجعله الله صدقة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p96/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p96/r2.speaker: الجمهور من العشرة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p96/r2.claim: The majority of the ten readers pronounce taṣṣaddaqu with a doubled ṣād, from tataṣaddaqu by assimilation of the second tāʾ into ṣād.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p96/r2.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور من العشرة { تصدقوا } بتشديد الصاد على أن أصله تتصدقوا فقلبت التاء الثانية صادا لتقاربهما وأدغمت في الصاد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p96/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p96/r3.speaker: عاصم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p96/r3.claim: Asim reads the ṣād lightly, deleting one of the two tāʾs for ease of pronunciation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p96/r3.anchor: وقرأه عاصم بتخفيف الصاد على حذف إحدى التاءين للتخفيف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p81/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p81/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p81/r1.claim: The surah is Medinan, revealed at different times; Ibn ʿAṭiyya identifies the verse warning of return to God as the last revelation to the Prophet.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p81/r1.anchor: هذه السورة مدنية، نزلت في مدد شتى، وفيها آخر آية نزلت على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، وهي:

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p81/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p81/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p81/r2.claim: Baqara is called the Qurʾān’s tent because of its stature and beauty and the legal rulings and exhortations it contains.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p81/r2.anchor: ويقال لسورة البقرة: «فسطاط القرآن» وذلك لعظمها وبهائها وما تضمنت من الأحكام والمواعظ

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p81/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p81/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p81/r3.claim: Ibn ʿUmar learned the surah’s jurisprudence and all its sciences over eight years.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p81/r3.anchor: وتعلمها عبد الله بن عمر رضي الله عنهما بفقهها وجميع ما تحتوي عليه من العلوم في ثمانية أعوام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p81/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p81/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p81/r4.claim: The surah is said to contain five hundred rulings and fifteen parables.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p81/r4.anchor: وفيها خمسمائة حكم، وخمسة عشر مثلا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p81/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p81/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p81/r5.claim: In a report transmitted by al-Ḥasan ibn Abī al-Ḥasan, the Prophet names al-Baqara the best surah and Ayat al-Kursī the best verse.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p81/r5.anchor: وروى الحسن بن أبي الحسن أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «أي القرآن أفضل؟»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p81/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p81/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p81/r6.claim: It is said that the meanings of its verses of mercy, hope, and punishment reach three hundred and sixty.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p81/r6.anchor: ويقال إن آيات الرحمة والرجاء والعذاب تنتهي فيها معانيها إلى ثلاثمائة وستين معنى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p81/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p81/r7.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p81/r7.claim: A report says the Prophet was given al-Baqara from the earlier scripture, Ṭā Hā and the Ṭawāsīn from Moses’s tablets, and al-Fātiḥa and the surah’s closing verses from beneath the Throne.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p81/r7.anchor: أعطيت سورة البقرة من الذكر الأول، وأعطيت طه والطواسين من ألواح موسى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p81/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p81/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p81/r8.claim: An authentic hadith says al-Baqara and Āl ʿImrān will come at resurrection as paired canopies or clouds, or rows of birds, defending their reciter.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p81/r8.anchor: في الحديث الصحيح عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال: «تجيء البقرة وآل عمران يوم القيامة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p81/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p81/r9.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p81/r9.claim: Al-Bukhārī transmits that reciting the final two verses of al-Baqara at night suffices the reader.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p81/r9.anchor: وفي البخاري أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام قال: «من قرأ بالآيتين من آخر سورة البقرة في ليلة كفتاه»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p81/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p81/r10.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p81/r10.claim: Abū Hurayra reports the Prophet saying that Satan does not enter a house where al-Baqara is recited.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p81/r10.anchor: وروى أبو هريرة عنه صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال: «البيت الذي تقرأ فيه سورة البقرة لا يدخله الشيطان»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p81/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p81/r11.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p81/r11.claim: A report calls al-Baqara the Qurʾān’s summit and Ayat al-Kursī its foremost verse, just as every thing has a summit.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p81/r11.anchor: لكل شيء سنام وسنام القرآن سورة البقرة، فيها آية هي سيدة أي القرآن هي آية الكرسي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p81/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p81/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p81/r12.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya gives the surah’s verse count as 285, while reporting alternatives of 286 and 287.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p81/r12.anchor: وعدد آي سورة البقرة مائتان وخمس وثمانون آية، وقيل: ست وثمانون، وقيل سبع وثمانون

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p376/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p376/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p376/r1.claim: The law gives creditors their principal when debtors can pay, but gives an insolvent debtor time until financial ease.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p376/r1.anchor: حكم الله تعالى لأرباب الربا برؤوس الأموال عند الواجدين للمال، ثم حكم في ذي العسرة بالنظرة إلى حالة اليسر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p376/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p376/r2.speaker: بعض العلماء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p376/r2.claim: Some scholars say this verse abrogated the pre-Islamic practice of selling an insolvent debtor for his debt.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p376/r2.anchor: هذه الآية ناسخة لما كان في الجاهلية من بيع من أعسر بدين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p376/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p376/r3.speaker: مكي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p376/r3.claim: Makkī transmits that the Prophet ordered this practice early in Islam.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p376/r3.anchor: أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أمر به في صدر الإسلام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p376/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p376/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p376/r4.claim: If the Prophet’s action is established, the ruling is abrogating; if not, it is not abrogation.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p376/r4.anchor: فإن ثبت فعل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فهو نسخ، وإلا فليس بنسخ

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p376/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p376/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p376/r5.claim: ʿUsra is hardship caused by lack of money; naẓira means deferment, and maysara is a verbal noun meaning ease.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p376/r5.anchor: ضيق الحال من جهة عدم المال ومنه جيش العسرة، والنظرة التأخير

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p376/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p376/r6.speaker: سيبويه وأبو علي وغيرهما
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p376/r6.claim: They parse dhū ʿusra as the subject of complete kāna, meaning “exists” or “occurs”; this implies wealth is the default and insolvency an emergent state that must be established.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p376/r6.anchor: وارتفع ذو عسرة ب كان التامة التي هي بمعنى وجد وحدث

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p376/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p376/r7.speaker: بعض الكوفيين
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p376/r7.claim: Some Kufans, as reported by al-Tabari, take kāna as defective with an omitted predicate, and take “then deferment” as the predicate of an implied subject such as “the ruling.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p376/r7.anchor: بل هي كان الناقصة والخبر محذوف، تقديره وإن كان من غرمائكم ذو عسرة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p376/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p376/r8.speaker: الطبري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p376/r8.claim: Al-Tabari says Ubay’s codex reads “if the debtor is insolvent,” using “the one sought” as the referent.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p376/r8.anchor: وفي مصحف أبي بن كعب: وإن كان ذو عسرة على معنى وإن كان المطلوب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p376/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p376/r9.speaker: الأعمش
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p376/r9.claim: Al-Aʿmash reads “if he is insolvent, then deferment.”

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p376/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p376/r10.speaker: أبو عمرو الداني عن أحمد بن موسى
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p376/r10.claim: Al-Dani transmits the same reading in Ubay’s codex.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p376/r10.anchor: وكذلك في مصحف أبي بن كعب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p376/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p376/r11.speaker: مكي والنقاش
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p376/r11.claim: They say the “debtor” wording confines the verse to usury debts, whereas the common reading with waw applies generally to all debtors.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p376/r11.anchor: وعلى هذا يختص لفظ الآية بأهل الربا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p376/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p376/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p376/r12.claim: The author says that distinction between the readings’ scope is not necessary.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p376/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p376/r13.speaker: المهدوي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p376/r13.claim: Al-Mahdawi reports that the Uthmanic codex has “fa-in kāna” with fāʾ before “debtor.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p376/r13.anchor: في مصحف عثمان، «فإن كان» بالفاء ذو عسرة بالواو

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p376/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p376/r14.speaker: جمهور القراء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p376/r14.claim: The standard reading pronounces naẓira with a kasra on the ẓāʾ.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p376/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p376/r15.speaker: مجاهد وأبو رجاء والحسن والضحاك
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p376/r15.claim: They read naẓra with a sukūn on the ẓāʾ, a Tamimi dialect form, like their forms for “karuma,” “kabid,” and “katif.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p376/r15.anchor: وهي على تسكين الظاء من نظرة، وهي لغة تميمية

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p376/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p376/r16.speaker: عطاء بن أبي رباح
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p376/r16.claim: Ata reads nāẓira on the fāʿila pattern; al-Zajjaj treats it as a verbal noun, like Quranic kādhiba, fāqira, and khāʾinat al-aʿyun.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p376/r16.anchor: على وزن فاعلة، وقال الزجاج: هي من أسماء المصادر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p377/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p377/r1.speaker: نافع
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p377/r1.claim: Nafiʿ alone reads maysira with a ḍamma on the sīn; the other readers and most people use a fatḥa, the more common Arabic pattern.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p377/r1.anchor: بضم السين، وقرأ باقي السبعة وجمهور الناس

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p377/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p377/r2.speaker: أبو علي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p377/r2.claim: Abu ʿAli notes that Arabic has forms like masruba and mashraba, but the pattern with fatḥa is more common.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p377/r2.anchor: قد قالوا: مسربة ومشربة، ولكن مفعلة بفتح العين أكثر في كلامهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p377/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p377/r3.speaker: عطاء بن أبي رياح ومجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p377/r3.claim: They read “then defer him until his ease” as an imperative, with the pronoun referring to the debtor; nāẓirahu means defer him.
