IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p377/r3.anchor: على الأمر في «ناظره» وجعلا الهاء ضمير الغريم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p377/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p377/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p377/r4.claim: The imperative nāẓirahu is the active form of deferment, as in sāmiḥahu, “pardon him.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p377/r4.anchor: فأما ناظره ففاعله من التأخير، كما تقول: سامحه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p377/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p377/r5.speaker: سيبويه
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p377/r5.claim: Sibawayh says the singular form mufʿil does not occur in Arabic; Abu ʿAli clarifies he means singulars.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p377/r5.anchor: قال سيبويه: ليس في الكلام مفعل، قال أبو علي يريد في الآحاد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p377/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p377/r6.speaker: عدي بن زيد وجميل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p377/r6.claim: Poetic examples include mālika and maʿūna forms, which Ibn Jinni treats as elided feminine singulars while Abu ʿAli allows that they are plurals.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p377/r6.anchor: أبلغ النعمان عني مألكا ... أنه قد طال حبسي وانتظار

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p377/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p377/r7.speaker: القاضي أبو محمد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p377/r7.claim: If maysir is a plural of maysara, it follows those poetic examples; as a singular it is irregular, but some people’s criticism is contradicted by Sibawayh’s discussion.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p377/r7.anchor: فإن كان ميسر جمع ميسرة فيجري مجرى هذه الأمثلة، وإن كان قارئه أراد به الإفراد فذلك شاذ

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p377/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p377/r8.speaker: ابن عباس وشريح
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p377/r8.claim: They restrict the deferment ruling to usury; other debts and trusts must be paid, except that manifest poverty necessarily requires deferment.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p377/r8.anchor: ذلك في الربا خاصة، وأما الديون وسائر الأمانات فليس فيها نظرة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p377/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p377/r9.speaker: جمهور العلماء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p377/r9.claim: The majority apply deferment to every insolvent debtor, whether the debt is usury, a trade debt, or a trust; al-Dahhak explains it this way.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p377/r9.anchor: النظرة إلى الميسرة حكم ثابت في المعسر سواء كان الدين ربا أو من تجارة في ذمة أو من أمانة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p377/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p377/r10.speaker: السدي وابن زيد والضحاك وجمهور الناس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p377/r10.claim: They understand “if you remit” as an exhortation to forgive an insolvent debtor, which is better than granting more time.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p377/r10.anchor: وندب الله تعالى بهذه الألفاظ إلى الصدقة على المعسر وجعل ذلك خيرا من إنظاره

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p377/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p377/r11.speaker: الطبري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p377/r11.claim: Al-Tabari reports another interpretation: giving charity to either rich or poor is better, but the author says cited reports from Qatada and Ibrahim do not support that framing and the verse does not include the rich.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p377/r11.anchor: معنى الآية وأن تصدقوا على الغني والفقير خير لكم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p377/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p377/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p377/r12.claim: The author rejects including rich people in the verse’s charity exhortation; the cited reports fit the majority’s reading instead.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p377/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p377/r13.speaker: جمهور القراء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p377/r13.claim: Most readers pronounce taṣaddaqū with a doubled ṣād through assimilation.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p377/r13.anchor: بتشديد الصاد على الإدغام من تتصدقوا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p377/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p377/r14.speaker: عاصم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p377/r14.claim: ʿAsim reads taṣaddaqū with a light ṣād; Ibn Masʿud’s codex has the unassimilated form.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p377#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p377#2/r1.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p377#2/r1.claim: Saʿid ibn al-Musayyib transmits ʿUmar saying the usury verse was the last revealed; the Prophet died without explaining it, so people should leave usury and doubtful matters.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p377#2/r1.anchor: كان آخر ما أنزل من القرآن آية الربا، وقبض رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ولم يفسرها لنا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p377#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p377#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p377#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas also says the usury verse was the last to be revealed.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p377#2/r2.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: آخر ما نزل آية الربا

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p99/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p99/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p99/r1.claim: Naẓira means waiting or granting time to the debtor.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p99/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p99/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p99/r2.claim: Forgiving the debt owed by an insolvent person is better for the creditor.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p334#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p334#2/r1.speaker: ابن السائب، مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p334#2/r1.claim: They report that after the command to abandon usury, Banu Amr ibn Umayr demanded principal from Banu al-Mughira; the latter pleaded hardship, and this verse was revealed.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p334#2/r1.anchor: ذكر ابن السائب و مقاتل أنه لم نزل قوله تعالى ﴿ وذروا ما بقي من الربا ﴾ قال بنو عمرو بن عمير لبني المغيرة هاتوا رؤوس أموالنا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p334#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p334#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p334#2/r2.claim: Hardship here means poverty and straitened circumstances.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p334#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p334#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p334#2/r3.claim: Most readers leave the sīn of ʿusra unvowelled; Abu Ja'far vowels it with damma here and in “the hour of hardship.”
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p334#2/r3.anchor: والجمهور على تسكين السين وضمها أبو جعفر هاهنا وفي ﴿ ساعة العسرة ﴾

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p334#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p334#2/r4.speaker: نافع، زيد عن يعقوب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p334#2/r4.claim: Most read the sīn of maysara with fatha; Nafi and Zayd from Yaqub use damma, with an additional variant in the ending and connection.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p334#2/r4.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور بفتح سين الميسرة وضمها نافع وتابعه زيد عن يعقوب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p334#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p334#2/r5.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p334#2/r5.claim: Al-Zajjaj explains “if it is” as “if it occurs,” and glosses nazira as postponement.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p334#2/r5.anchor: قال الزجاج ومعنى و إن كان وإن وقع والنظرة التأخير

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p334#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p334#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p334#2/r6.claim: The creditor must defer the principal, after the usury is relinquished, when the debtor is insolvent; giving charity to the debtor is better.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p334#2/r6.anchor: فأمرهم بتأخير رأس المال بعد إسقاط الربا إذا كان المطالب معسرا وأعلمهم أن الصدقة عليه بذلك أفضل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p334#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p334#2/r7.speaker: عاصم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p334#2/r7.claim: Most readers double the ṣād in “that you give charity”; Asim lightens the ṣād while doubling the dāl.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p334#2/r7.anchor: والأكثرون على تشديد الصاد وخففها عاصم مع تشديد الدال

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p334#2/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p334#2/r8.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p334#2/r8.claim: Ibn Abi Abla reads the ṣād with sukūn and the dāl with damma, deriving the form from truthfulness.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p334#2/r8.anchor: وسكنها ابن أبي عبلة مع ضم الدال فجعله من الصدق

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p717#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p717#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p717#2/r1.claim: God commands creditors to give an insolvent debtor time until he can pay, unlike the pre-Islamic creditor's demand to pay at once or increase the debt through usury.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p717#2/r1.anchor: يأمر تعالى بالصبر على المعسر الذي لا يجد وفاء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p717#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p717#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p717#2/r2.claim: The verse encourages a creditor to waive the entire principal and promises great good and reward for doing so.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p717#2/r2.anchor: وأن تتركوا رأس المال بالكلية وتضعوه عن المدين

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p717#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p717#2/r3.speaker: رسول الله
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p717#2/r3.claim: Abu Umama reports that whoever wants God's shade on the day without shade should ease an insolvent debtor's burden or waive the debt.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p717#2/r3.anchor: من سره أن يظله الله يوم لا ظل إلا ظله، فلييسر على معسر أو ليضع عنه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p717#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p717#2/r4.speaker: رسول الله
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p717#2/r4.claim: Burayda reports that before a debt comes due, each day of delay earns charity equal to the debt; after it falls due, each day of delay earns double that amount.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p717#2/r4.anchor: له بكل يوم مثله صدقة قبل أن يحل الدين، فإذا حل الدين فأنظره، فله بكل يوم مثلاه صدقة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p717#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p717#2/r5.speaker: رسول الله
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p717#2/r5.claim: Abu Qatada found his debtor hiding because he was insolvent; he wept and reported the Prophet's promise of the Throne's shade for one who relieves or erases a debtor's obligation. Muslim records it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p717#2/r5.anchor: من نفس عن غريمه -أو محا عنه -كان في ظل العرش يوم القيامة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p718/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p718/r1.speaker: رسول الله
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p718/r1.claim: A man who eased solvent buyers and delayed insolvent ones is told by God that He is more entitled to ease and is admitted to Paradise; Bukhari, Muslim, and Ibn Majah transmit it, with Muslim adding Uqba ibn Amir and Abu Masud to the report.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p718/r1.anchor: أنا أحق من ييسر، ادخل الجنة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p718/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p718/r2.speaker: رسول الله
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p718/r2.claim: A merchant instructed his servants to overlook insolvent buyers in hope that God would overlook him, and God forgave him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p718/r2.anchor: كان تاجر يداين الناس، فإذا رأى معسرا قال لفتيانه: تجاوزوا عنه، لعل الله يتجاوز عنا، فتجاوز الله عنه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p718/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p718/r3.speaker: رسول الله
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p718/r3.claim: Sahl ibn Hunayf reports that helping a fighter, an insolvent debtor, or an enslaved person buying freedom earns God's shade on the day without shade; al-Hakim calls its chain sound and says the two collectors did not include it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p718/r3.anchor: من أعان مجاهدا في سبيل الله أو غازيا، أو غارما في عسرته، أو مكاتبا في رقبته، أظله الله (1) يوم لا ظل إلا ظله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p718/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p718/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p718/r4.claim: Al-Hakim grades the Sahl ibn Hunayf report's chain as sound and notes that Bukhari and Muslim did not record it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p718/r4.anchor: ثم قال: صحيح الإسناد، ولم يخرجاه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p718/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p718/r5.speaker: رسول الله
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p718/r5.claim: Ibn Umar reports that someone seeking an answered prayer and relief from distress should ease an insolvent debtor; Ahmad alone transmits the report.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p718/r5.anchor: من أراد أن تستجاب دعوته، وأن تكشف كربته، فليفرج عن معسر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p718/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p718/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p718/r6.claim: Ibn Kathir notes that Ahmad alone transmits the Ibn Umar report.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p719/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p719/r1.speaker: رسول الله
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p719/r1.claim: Abu Masud reports a man who could name no good deed except easing solvent buyers and delaying insolvent ones; God says He is more entitled to do so and forgives him. Muslim also transmits this through Abu Malik Saad ibn Tariq.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p719/r1.anchor: نحن أولى بذلك منك، تجاوزوا عن عبدي. فغفر له

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p719/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p719/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p719/r2.claim: Ibn Kathir says the route for the Imran ibn Husayn report is unusual and notes that a similar report from Burayda was given earlier.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p719/r2.anchor: غريب من هذا الوجه وقد تقدم عن بريدة نحوه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p719/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p719/r3.speaker: رسول الله
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p719/r3.claim: Imran ibn Husayn reports that each day a creditor delays a debt owed by someone earns charity equal to the debt.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p719/r3.anchor: من كان له على رجل حق فأخره (9) كان له بكل يوم صدقة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p719/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p719/r4.speaker: رسول الله
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p719/r4.claim: Abu al-Yusr reports that delaying an insolvent debtor or waiving the debt earns God's shade on the day without shade; Muslim transmits another route through Ubada ibn al-Walid.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p719/r4.anchor: من أنظر معسرا أو وضع عنه أظله الله، عز وجل، في ظله يوم لا ظل إلا ظله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p719/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p719/r5.speaker: أبو اليسر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p719/r5.claim: When his debtor admitted insolvency and explained he feared lying or breaking a promise, Abu al-Yusr erased the debt record and released him if unable to pay, then testified that he heard the Prophet promise divine shade for delaying or waiving a debt.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p719/r5.anchor: فأتى بصحيفته فمحاها بيده، ثم قال: فإن وجدت قضاء فاقضني، وإلا فأنت في حل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p720/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p720/r1.speaker: رسول الله
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p720/r1.claim: Uthman reports that God shades a person who delays an insolvent debtor or releases a debtor from what is owed.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p720/r1.anchor: أظل الله عينا في ظله، يوم لا ظل إلا ظله من أنظر معسرا، أو ترك لغارم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p720/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p720/r2.speaker: رسول الله
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p720/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas reports promises for delaying or waiving an insolvent person's debt, including protection from Hell; the report also says Paradise's deeds are arduous, Hell's deeds easy, the fortunate are protected from trials, and restraining anger fills the heart with faith.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p720/r2.anchor: من أنظر معسرا أو وضع له، وقاه الله من فيح جهنم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p720/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p720/r3.speaker: رسول الله
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p720/r3.claim: A second Ibn Abbas report says that God will grant respite regarding a debtor's sin until the debtor repents if the creditor delays payment until the debtor can pay.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p720/r3.anchor: من أنظر معسرا إلى ميسرته أنظره الله بذنبه إلى توبته

NAHHAS:v1p341/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p341/r3.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p341/r3.claim: كان means ‘occurred’; Sibawayh's poetic example supports this and makes the interpretation general. Alternatively, the predicate is omitted, meaning ‘if a debtor is in hardship.’
NAHHAS:v1p341/r3.anchor: كان بمعنى وقع وأنشد سيبويه ( فدى لبني ذهل بن شيبان ناقتي … إذا كان يوم ذو كواكب أشهب ) فهذا أحسن ما قيل فيه

NAHHAS:v1p341/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p341/r4.speaker: سيبويه
NAHHAS:v1p341/r4.claim: His poem has إذا كان يوم ذو كواكب أشهب, using كان in the sense of an event occurring.
NAHHAS:v1p341/r4.anchor: ( فدى لبني ذهل بن شيبان ناقتي … إذا كان يوم ذو كواكب أشهب )

NAHHAS:v1p341/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p341/r5.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p341/r5.claim: Abdullah's codex reads وإن كان ذا عسرة; Nahhas estimates ‘if the person you deal with is in hardship.’
NAHHAS:v1p341/r5.anchor: وقال حجاج الوراق في مصحف عبد الله ( وإن كان ذا عسرة ) قال أبو جعفر والتقدير وإن كان المعامل ذا عسرة

NAHHAS:v1p341/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p341/r6.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p341/r6.claim: فنظرة إلى ميسرة means to grant respite to the person owed money.
NAHHAS:v1p341/r6.anchor: ( فنظرة إلى ميسرة ) أي فالذي تعاملون به نظرة

NAHHAS:v1p341/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p341/r7.speaker: الحسن وأبو رجاء
NAHHAS:v1p341/r7.claim: They read فنظرة إلى ميسرة with the kasra omitted as too heavy.
NAHHAS:v1p341/r7.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وأبو رجاء ( فنظرة إلى ميسرة ) حذف الكسرة لثقلها

NAHHAS:v1p341/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p341/r8.speaker: مجاهد وعطاء
NAHHAS:v1p341/r8.claim: They read فناظره as an imperative, followed by إلى ميسرة with ḍamma on sīn, kasra on rāʾ, and hāʾ retained in connected speech.
NAHHAS:v1p341/r8.anchor: وقرأ مجاهد وعطاء ( فناظره ) على الأمر ( إلى ميسرة ) بضم السين وكسر الراء

NAHHAS:v1p341/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p341/r9.speaker: أبو إسحاق
NAHHAS:v1p341/r9.claim: He reports فناظرة إلى ميسرة and allows it as a verbal noun, like ليس لوقعتها كاذبة.
NAHHAS:v1p341/r9.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق وقرىء ( فناظرة إلى ميسرة )

NAHHAS:v1p341/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p341/r11.speaker: أبو حاتم
NAHHAS:v1p341/r11.claim: He rejects فناظرة here, reserving that form for the woman in 27:35; this verse means deferment, as in أنظرتك بالدين. Abū Isḥāq allows it as a verbal noun.
NAHHAS:v1p341/r11.anchor: قال أبو حاتم ولا يجوز فناظرة إنما ذلك في النمل فناظرة بم يرجع المرسلون لأنها امرأة تكلمت

NAHHAS:v1p341/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p341/r12.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p341/r12.claim: ميسرة with fatḥa is the most eloquent Najdi form; kasra is a rare Hijazi form. Nahhas calls one reading ungrammatical, though Akhfash says it is more plausible by analogy with common مفعل and allows موسرة.
NAHHAS:v1p341/r12.anchor: قال أبو جعفر ميسرة أفصح اللغات وهي لغة أهل نجد و ميسرة وإن كانت لغة أهل الحجاز فهي من الشواذ

NAHHAS:v1p341/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p341/r13.speaker: الأخفش سعيد
NAHHAS:v1p341/r13.claim: He says إلى ميسرة is more plausible, citing the common pattern مجلس, and also allows إلى موسرة.
NAHHAS:v1p341/r13.anchor: قال الأخفش سعيد ولو قرءوا إلى ميسرة لكان أشبه والذي قال الأخفش حسن

NAHHAS:v1p341/r14.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p341/r14.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p341/r14.claim: وأن تصدقوا خير لكم is subject and predicate; Abdullah's codex has وأن تتصدقوا; ʿĪsā and Ṭalḥa read a lightened form, deleting tāʾ or assimilating it into ṣād.
NAHHAS:v1p341/r14.anchor: ( وأن تصدقوا خير لكم ) ابتداء وخبر وفي قراءة عبد الله ( وأن تتصدقوا )

NAHHAS:v1p341/r15.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p341/r15.speaker: عيسى وطلحة
NAHHAS:v1p341/r15.claim: They read وأن تصدقوا with a lightened form; tāʾ assimilates into ṣād because the letters are close, unlike the distant tāʾ and fāʾ in تتفكرون.
NAHHAS:v1p341/r15.anchor: وقرأ عيسى وطلحة ( وأن تصدقوا ) مخففا تتصدقوا على الأصل وتصدقوا تدغم التاء في الصاد

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p349#3/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p349#3/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p349#3/r4.claim: A debtor's hardship means insolvency; ʿUthman reads the phrase with the accusative ذا, explicitly making the debtor the subject.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p349#3/r4.anchor: وإن وقع غريم من غرمائكم ذو عسرة أو ذو إعسار

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p349#3/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p349#3/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p349#3/r5.claim: Another reading says whoever is insolvent should be granted deferment, with an implied ruling or command meaning postponement.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p349#3/r5.anchor: وقرىء ومن كان ذا عسرة فنظرة أي فالحكم أو فالأمر نظرة وهي الإنظار

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p349#3/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p349#3/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p349#3/r6.claim: The noun for deferment is also read with a still ẓāʾ; ʿAṭāʾ reads it as the creditor who waits or grants respite.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p349#3/r6.anchor: وقرىء ( فنظرة ) بسكون الظاء وقرا عطاء ( فناظره ) بمعنى فصاحب الحق ناظره أي منتظره

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p349#3/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p349#3/r7.speaker: عطاء
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p349#3/r7.claim: ʿAṭāʾ also reads the phrase as an imperative to be lenient and grant the debtor more time.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p349#3/r7.anchor: وعنه فناظره على الأمر بمعنى فسامحه بالنظرة وياسره بها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p350/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p350/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p350/r1.claim: ميسرة means financial ease or solvency; it is read with a ḍamma on the sīn, like the paired forms maqbara and mashriqa.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p350/r1.anchor: إلى يسار وقرىء بضم السين كمقبرة ومقبرة ومشرقة ومشرقة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p350/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p350/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p350/r2.claim: The paired forms may be annexed with the tāʾ omitted; Zamakhsharī cites a poetic line and Qur'an 24:37 as parallels.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p350/r2.anchor: وقرىء بهما مضافين بحذف التاء عند الإضافة كقوله ( وأخلفوك عدا الأمر الذي وعدوا )

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p350/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p350/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p350/r3.claim: The verse encourages creditors to forgive all or part of the principal owed by insolvent debtors, as also urged in 2:237.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p350/r3.anchor: ندب إلى ان يتصدقوا برؤس اموالهم على من أعسر من غرمائهم أو ببعضها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p350/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p350/r4.speaker: النبي
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p350/r4.claim: A Prophetic report offers a second interpretation: a creditor who defers a Muslim's debt receives charity for every day of delay.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p350/r4.anchor: لقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم 152 ( لا يحل دين رجل مسلم فيؤخره الا كان له بكل يوم صدقة )

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p350/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p350/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p350/r5.claim: If people know that forgiving the debt is better for them but do not act, they are treated as though they did not know.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p350/r5.anchor: إنه خير لكم فتعملوا به جعل من لا يعمل به وإن علمه كأنه لا يعلمه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p350/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p350/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p350/r6.claim: A reading lightens the ṣād in تصدقوا by omitting the second tāʾ.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p350/r6.anchor: وقرىء ( تصدقوا ) بتخفيف الصاد على حذف التاء

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p351/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p351/r14.speaker: أبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p351/r14.claim: A reported reading of the insolvent-debtor phrase is “if he is in hardship,” using the accusative; this is permissible Arabic.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p351/r14.anchor: قيل إن في قراءة أبي { ذا عسرة } وهو جائز في العربية .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p351/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p351/r15.speaker: ابن عباس، شريح
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p351/r15.claim: One view makes postponement mandatory only for an insolvent debtor owing a usurious debt.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p351/r15.anchor: أن الإنظار بالعسرة واجب في دين الربا خاصة , قاله ابن عباس , وشريح .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p351/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p351/r16.speaker: عطاء، الضحاك
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p351/r16.claim: Another view applies the mandatory delay to every debt, based on the verse's general wording.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p351/r16.anchor: أنه عام يجب إنظاره بالعسرة في كل دين , لظاهر الآية , وهو قول عطاء , والضحاك

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p351/r17.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p351/r17.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p351/r17.claim: A reconciliation applies the explicit text to usurious debts and extends the same rule to other debts by analogy.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p351/r17.anchor: وقيل إن الإنظار بالعسرة في دين الربا بالنص , وفي غيره من الديون بالقياس .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p351/r18.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p351/r18.speaker: الأكثرون
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p351/r18.claim: The phrase “until ease” derives from yusr and means until the debtor becomes solvent; this is the majority view.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p351/r18.anchor: مفعلة من اليسر , وهو أن يوسر , وهو قول الأكثرين .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p351/r19.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p351/r19.speaker: إبراهيم النخعي
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p351/r19.claim: Another interpretation reads “until ease” as postponement until death.

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p351/r20.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p351/r20.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p351/r20.claim: Forgiving an insolvent debtor's debt is better than merely granting more time.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p351/r20.anchor: يعني وأن تصدقوا على المعسر بما عليه من الدين خير لكم من أن تنظروه

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p351/r21.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p351/r21.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p351/r21.claim: ʿUmar said the usury verse was the last Qur'anic revelation and urged people to abandon usury; the Prophet died before explaining it.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p351/r21.anchor: عن عمر بن الخطاب قال : كان آخر ما نزل من القرآن آية الربا , فدعوا الربا والربية

MUJAHID:v1p118/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p118/r1.speaker: شريح
MUJAHID:v1p118/r1.claim: Shurayh says this instruction concerns debt when the debtor is in hardship.
MUJAHID:v1p118/r1.anchor: عن شريح في قوله ﴿ وإن كان ذو عسرة فنظرة إلى ميسرة ﴾ قال هذا في الدين

MUQATIL:2:278-280/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:278-280/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:278-280/r5.claim: The Prophet sent the verse to Attab, who read it to Banu Amr ibn Umayr; they repented and sought their principal, but Banu al-Mughira pleaded hardship, prompting the order to grant a debtor in hardship more time.
MUQATIL:2:278-280/r5.anchor: فبعث النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم بهذه الآية إلى عتاب بن أسيد بمكة،

MUQATIL:2:278-280/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:278-280/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:278-280/r6.claim: A debtor in hardship—here Banu al-Mughira—must be given time until becoming solvent; “grant me respite” in 7:14 means give me a delay.
MUQATIL:2:278-280/r6.anchor: يعنى بنى المغيرة، { فنظرة إلى ميسرة } ، يقول: فأجله إلى غناه،

MUQATIL:2:280-281/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:280-281/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:280-281/r1.claim: Forgiving the entire debt owed by insolvent Banu al-Mughira is better than collecting it.
MUQATIL:2:280-281/r1.anchor: { وأن تصدقوا } به كله على بنى المغيرة وهم معسرون، فلا تأخذونه،

NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#2/r1.claim: If a debtor is insolvent, the ruling or command is to grant time until solvency; maysara has two language forms, one read by Nafi'.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#2/r1.anchor: وقع غريم من غرمائكم ذو عسرة ذو إعسار

NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#2/r2.speaker: عاصم
NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#2/r2.claim: Asim reads the verb with lightening, meaning creditors remit all or part of the principal for an insolvent debtor; other readers use the assimilated, doubled form.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#2/r2.anchor: بالتخفيف عاصم أى تتصدقوا برؤس أموالكم أو ببعضها على من أعسر

NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#2/r3.claim: The light reading omits one of the two tāʾs; the heavier reading assimilates them.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#2/r3.anchor: فالتخفيف على حذف إحدى التاءين والتشديد على الإدغام

NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#2/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#2/r4.claim: Another interpretation takes charity to mean granting the insolvent debtor more time; a Prophetic report says delaying an owed debt earns charity for every day.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#2/r4.anchor: وقيل أريد بالتصدق الإنظار لقوله عليه السلام لا يحل دين رجل مسلم فيؤخره إلا كان له بكل يوم صدقة

NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#2/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#2/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#2/r5.claim: If people know this is better for them and fail to act, they are treated as if they do not know.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#2/r5.anchor: جعل من لا يعمل به و إن علمه كأنه لا يعلمه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:280/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280/r1.claim: When Thaqif demanded principal from Banu al-Mughira, the latter pleaded poverty and asked to wait until their harvest; this verse was revealed.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280/r1.anchor: وذلك أن ثقيفا لما طلبوا أموالهم التي لهم على بني المغيرة شكوا العسرة يعني بني المغيرة وقالوا: ليس لنا شيء، وطلبوا الأجل إلى وقت ثمارهم فنزلت هذه الآية

QURTUBI-FULL:2:280/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280/r2.claim: Together with 2:279, the verse establishes a creditor’s right to demand principal and take the debtor’s property without consent; the debtor must therefore repay when able.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280/r2.anchor: مع قوله: { وإن تبتم فلكم رؤوس أموالكم } يدل على ثبوت المطالبة لصاحب الدين على المدين وجواز أخذ ماله بغير رضاه.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:280/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280/r3.speaker: بعض العلماء ومكي وابن عطية
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280/r3.claim: Some scholars say the verse abrogated the pre-Islamic practice of selling insolvent debtors; Makki says the Prophet ordered that practice early in Islam, and Ibn Atiyya says abrogation follows only if that Prophetic act is established.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280/r3.anchor: قال المهدوي وقال بعض العلماء: هذه الآية ناسخة لما كان في الجاهلية من بيع من أعسر. وحكى مكي أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أمر به في صدر الإسلام.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:280/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280/r4.speaker: الطحاوي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280/r4.claim: Al-Tahawi says a free person who lacked property could be sold for debt in early Islam until this verse abrogated the practice.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280/r4.anchor: قال الطحاوي: كان الحر يباع في الدين أول الإسلام إذا لم يكن له مال يقضيه عن نفسه حتى نسخ الله ذلك

QURTUBI-FULL:2:280/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280/r5.claim: A report used as evidence says a debtor was brought to the Prophet, who found no property and sold him for the debt; al-Bazzar transmits a longer version, but Muslim ibn Khalid and Ibn al-Baylamani are not reliable proof.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280/r5.anchor: ومسلم بن خالد الزنجي وعبد الرحمن بن البيلماني لا يحتج بهما.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:280/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280/r6.speaker: أبو هريرة والحسن وعامة الفقهاء
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280/r6.claim: Abu Hurayra, Hasan, and most jurists apply the deferment rule generally to every insolvent debtor.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280/r6.anchor: وقال جماعة من أهل العلم: قوله تعالى: { فنظرة إلى ميسرة } عامة في جميع الناس، فكل من أعسر أنظر

QURTUBI-FULL:2:280/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280/r7.speaker: النحاس وعطاء والضحاك والربيع بن خثيم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280/r7.claim: Al-Nahhas prefers the view of Ata, al-Dahhak, and al-Rabi ibn Khuthaym: every insolvent person is granted time in usury and all debts; this combines the positions, and the nominative reading supports generality.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:280/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280/r8.speaker: ابن عباس وشريح
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas and Shurayh limit the deferment rule to usury; for other debts and transactions, the debtor must pay or may be imprisoned until payment.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280/r8.anchor: وقال ابن عباس وشريح: ذلك في الربا خاصة فأما الديون وسائر المعاملات فليس فيها نظرة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#2/r1.claim: Ibn Atiyya says compelling payment would apply only when the debtor is not destitute; clear poverty necessarily requires a deferment.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن عطية: فكان هذا القول يترتب إذا لم يكن فقر مدقع، وأما مع العدم والفقر الصريح فالحكم هو النظرة ضرورة.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#2/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#2/r2.claim: When debtors’ debts accumulate, a judge may take all their property while leaving necessities; Malik’s report through Ibn Nafi says only enough clothing to cover the debtor must remain.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#2/r2.anchor: من كثرت ديونه وطلب غرماؤه مالهم فللحاكم أن يخلعه عن كل ماله ويترك له ما كان من ضرورته. روى ابن نافع عن مالك أنه لايترك له إلا ما يواريه.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#2/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#2/r3.claim: The well-known position leaves customary clothing without surplus and preserves a cloak if removing it would humiliate the debtor.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#2/r3.anchor: والمشهور أنه يترك له كسوته المعتاد ما لم يكن فيها فضل، ولا ينزع منه رداؤه إن كان ذلك مزريا به.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#2/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#2/r4.claim: Scholars differ on leaving clothing for the debtor’s wife and on selling books belonging to a learned person.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#2/r4.anchor: وفي ترك كسوة زوجته وفي بيع كتبه إن كان عالما خلاف.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#2/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#2/r5.claim: A debtor is not left a dwelling, servant, or Friday clothing unless these have little value; in such circumstances detention is forbidden.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#2/r5.anchor: ولا يترك له مسكن ولا خادم ولا ثوب جمعة ما لم تقل قيمتها وعند هذا يحرم حبسه.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#2/r6.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#2/r6.claim: Abu Said reports that after a fruit purchase left a man heavily indebted, the Prophet solicited donations, then told creditors to take what they found and no more.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#2/r6.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري قال: أصيب رجل في عهد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في ثمار ابتاعها فكثر دينه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#2/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#2/r7.claim: The report establishes that the Prophet did not imprison the insolvent debtor or require creditors to keep pursuing him; Shurayh identifies the man as Muadh ibn Jabal, against the Hanafi view of detention to discover hidden assets.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#2/r7.anchor: وهذا نص فلم يأمر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بحبس الرجل، وهو معاذ بن جبل كما قال شريح، ولا بملازمته، خلافا لأبي حنيفة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#2/r8.speaker: مالك والشافعي وأبو حنيفة وغيرهم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#2/r8.claim: These jurists detain a bankrupt debtor until insolvency is established; Malik does not detain one unless concealment or obstinacy is suspected, and not when genuine insolvency is verified.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#2/r8.anchor: ويحبس المفلس في قول مالك والشافعي وأبي حنيفة وغيرهم حتى يتبين عدمه.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#2/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#2/r9.claim: If collected assets are destroyed before sale and delivery to creditors, the debtor guarantees them and the creditors’ debts remain against him.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#2/r9.anchor: فعلى المفلس ضمانه، ودين الغرماء ثابت في ذمته.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#2/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#2/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#2/r10.claim: If a judge sells the debtor’s property and receives the proceeds, their loss before creditors collect them is borne by creditors and discharges the debtor.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#2/r10.anchor: كان عليهم ضمانه وقد برىء المفلس منه.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#2/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#2/r11.speaker: محمد بن عبد الحكم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#2/r11.claim: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hakam says the debtor remains liable for the proceeds until they reach the creditors.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#2/r11.anchor: وقال محمد بن عبد الحكم: ضمانه من المفلس أبدا حتى يصل إلى الغرماء.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#2/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#2/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#2/r12.claim: Usra means financial hardship, nathira means delay, and maysara is a verbal noun meaning ease.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#2/r12.anchor: العسرة ضيق الحال من جهة عدم المال ومنه جيش العسرة. والنظرة التأخير. والميسرة مصدر بمعنى اليسر.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#2/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#2/r13.speaker: سيبويه وأبو علي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#2/r13.claim: Sibawayh and Abu Ali parse “dhu” as nominative because kana here is complete and means “existed” or “occurred.”
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#2/r13.anchor: وارتفع «ذو» بكان التامة التي بمعنى وجد وحدث هذا قول سيبويه وأبي علي وغيرهما.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#3/r1.speaker: سيبويه
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#3/r1.claim: Sibawayh cites a poetic line with nominative dhu to illustrate the grammatical construction.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#3/r1.anchor: فدى لبني ذهل بن شيبان ناقتي إذا كان يوم ذو كواكب أشهب

QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#3/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#3/r2.claim: The accusative construction is also permissible; the Ubayy codex reads “if the debtor was insolvent” with accusative dhu.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#3/r2.anchor: ويجوز النصب. وفي مصحف أبي بن كعب «وإن كان ذا عسرة» على معنى وإن كان المطلوب ذا عسرة.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#3/r3.speaker: الأعمش وأبو عمرو الداني عن أحمد بن موسى
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#3/r3.claim: Al-Amash reads “if he is insolvent, then deferment”; Abu Amr al-Dani reports this reading from Ahmad ibn Musa and says it is also in Ubayy’s codex.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#3/r3.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش «وإن كان معسرا فنظرة». قال أبو عمرو الداني عن أحمد بن موسى: وكذلك في مصحف أبي بن كعب.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#3/r4.speaker: النحاس ومكي والنقاش
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#3/r4.claim: Al-Nahhas, Makki, and al-Naqqash say the alternative readings restrict the verse to usury debt, while the standard nominative reading covers all debts.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#3/r4.anchor: وعلى هذا يختص لفظ الآية بأهل الربا، وعلى من قرأ «ذو» فهي عامة في جميع من عليه دين

QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#3/r5.speaker: المهدوي والنحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#3/r5.claim: Al-Mahdawi reports an Uthman codex reading with fa before “dhu hardship”; al-Nahhas reports another Uthman codex reading using accusative “dhu.”
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#3/r5.anchor: وحكى المهدوي أن في مصحف عثمان «فإن كان بالفاء ذو عسرة». وروى المعتمر عن حجاج الوراق قال: في مصحف عثمان «وإن كان ذا عسرة»

QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#3/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#3/r6.speaker: مجاهد وأبو رجاء والحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#3/r6.claim: The standard reading has nathira with a kasra; Mujahid, Abu Raja, and Hasan read it with a silent dh, a Tamimi dialect form comparable to their pronunciations of karam and kabid.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#3/r6.anchor: وقرأ مجاهد وأبو رجاء والحسن «فنظرة» بسكون الظاء، وهي لغة تميمية

QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#3/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#3/r7.speaker: نافع
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#3/r7.claim: Nafi alone reads maysara with a damma on the sin; the majority read it with a fatha.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#3/r7.anchor: وقرأ نافع وحده «ميسرة» بضم السين، والجمهور بفتحها.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#3/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#3/r8.speaker: مجاهد وعطاء
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#3/r8.claim: Mujahid and Ata are reported to read “then defer it to the matter until ease,” with a damma on the sin, kasra on the ra, and the y retained in connected speech.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#3/r8.anchor: وحكى النحاس عن مجاهد وعطاء «فناظره على الأمر إلى ميسر» هي بضم السين وكسر الراء وإثبات الياء في الإدراج.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#3/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#3/r9.speaker: أبو حاتم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#3/r9.claim: Abu Hatim rejects the reading “fanazira,” which he says belongs only in 27:32 where a woman speaks of herself; here the word means deferment from the verb “to postpone.”
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#3/r9.anchor: قال أبو حاتم لا يجوز فناظرة، إنما ذلك في «النمل» لأنها امرأة تكلمت بهذا لنفسها

QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#3/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#3/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#3/r10.claim: Qurtubi links the deferment noun to the wording “grant me respite until the day they are resurrected.”
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#3/r10.anchor: ومنه قوله: فأنظرني إلى يوم يبعثون

QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#3/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#3/r11.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#3/r11.claim: Al-Zajjaj allows “fanazira,” analyzing it as a verbal noun, like the forms in 56:2, 75:25, and 40:19.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#3/r11.anchor: وأجاز ذلك أبو إسحاق الزجاج وقال: هي من أسماء المصادر كقوله تعالى: ليس لوقعتها كاذبة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#3/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#3/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#3/r12.claim: The phrase “and that you give charity” is the subject, and “is better” is its predicate.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#3/r12.anchor: قوله تعالى: { وأن تصدقوا } ابتداء، وخبره { خير }.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#3/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#3/r13.speaker: السدي وابن زيد والضحاك
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#3/r13.claim: Al-Suddi, Ibn Zayd, and al-Dahhak say God’s wording encourages charity to an insolvent debtor and makes it better than granting more time.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#3/r13.anchor: ندب الله تعالى بهذه الألفاظ إلى الصدقة على المعسر وجعل ذلك خيرا من إنظاره

QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#3/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#3/r14.speaker: الطبري
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#3/r14.claim: Al-Tabari transmits another view that charity to either rich or poor is better than deferment; Qurtubi prefers the first view because this verse does not concern the rich.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#3/r14.anchor: وقال الطبري: وقال آخرون: معنى الآية وأن تصدقوا على الغني والفقير خير لكم. والصحيح الأول، وليس في الآية مدخل للغني.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#3/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#3/r15.speaker: أبو جعفر الطحاوي عن بريدة بن الحصيب
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#3/r15.claim: Al-Tahawi begins transmitting a report from Burayda ibn al-Husayb in which the Prophet speaks; this chunk ends before the report’s content is given.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#3/r15.anchor: روى أبو جعفر الطحاوي عن بريدة بن الحصيب قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#4/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#4/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#4/r1.claim: A report promises one daily charity for each day a creditor gives an insolvent debtor respite before maturity, and double that daily reward for respite after maturity.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#4/r1.anchor: بكل يوم صدقة مالم يحل الدين فإذا أنظره بعد الحل فله بكل يوم مثله صدقة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#4/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#4/r2.speaker: أبو مسعود
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#4/r2.claim: The Prophet recounts a wealthy man whose only good deed was ordering his servants to overlook insolvent debtors; God says He is more entitled to do so and pardons him.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#4/r2.anchor: وروى مسلم عن أبي مسعود قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#4/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#4/r3.speaker: أبو قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#4/r3.claim: After finding a debtor who had hidden, Abu Qatada heard the Prophet promise rescue from Resurrection's distress to whoever relieves an insolvent person or remits the debt.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#4/r3.anchor: وروي عن أبي قتادة أنه طلب غريما له فتوارى عنه ثم وجده

QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#4/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#4/r4.speaker: أبو اليسر
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#4/r4.claim: The Prophet says that whoever gives an insolvent debtor respite or remits the debt will be shaded by God in His shade.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#4/r4.anchor: وفي حديث أبي اليسر الطويل واسمه كعب بن عمرو أنه سمع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول

QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#4/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#4/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#4/r5.claim: These reports explicitly encourage giving insolvent debtors relief.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#4/r5.anchor: ففي هذه الأحاديث من الترغيب ما هو منصوص فيها

QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#4/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#4/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#4/r6.claim: Abu Qatada's report establishes that a creditor who knows or suspects the debtor's insolvency may not demand payment, even without a judge's finding of insolvency.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#4/r6.anchor: وحديث أبي قتادة يدل على أن رب الدين إذا علم عسرة غريمه أو ظنها حرمت عليه مطالبته

QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#4/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#4/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#4/r7.claim: Giving respite means delaying collection until the debtor becomes solvent; remission means cancelling the debt from the debtor's liability.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#4/r7.anchor: وإنظار المعسر تأخيره إلى أن يوسر. والوضع عند إسقاط الدين عن ذمته.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#4/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#4/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#4/r8.claim: Abu al-Yusr combined respite and remission: he erased the debt record and told the debtor to repay if able, otherwise he was released from the debt.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#4/r8.anchor: وقد جمع المعنيين أبو اليسر لغريمه حيث محا عنه الصحيفة

SAMIN-DURR:2:280/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:280/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:280/r1.claim: The author prefers kāna as a complete verb meaning ‘occurred’ or ‘came to exist,’ taking the indefinite dhū ʿusratin as its subject; it often appears this way with an indefinite subject.
SAMIN-DURR:2:280/r1.anchor: في " كان " هذه وجهان، أحدهما: - وهو الأظهر - أنها تامة بمعنى حدث ووجد أي: وإن حدث ذو عسرة فتكتفي بفاعلها

SAMIN-DURR:2:280/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:280/r2.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:2:280/r2.claim: A second analysis makes kāna defective with an omitted predicate, such as ‘a debtor who owes you a right’; some Kufans specify that the person is one of the creditors’ debtors.
SAMIN-DURR:2:280/r2.anchor: والثاني: أنها الناقصة والخبر محذوف. قال أبو البقاء: " تقديره: وإن كان ذو عسرة لكم عليه حق أو نحو ذلك "

SAMIN-DURR:2:280/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:280/r3.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:2:280/r3.claim: The Shaykh says Basran grammarians do not allow an omitted predicate of kāna, because its predicate is doubly required as both a predicate and a complement of the preceding verb.
SAMIN-DURR:2:280/r3.anchor: قال الشيخ: " وحذف خبر كان " لا يجيزه أصحابنا لا اختصارا ولا اقتصارا

SAMIN-DURR:2:280/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:280/r4.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:2:280/r4.claim: The Shaykh answers the counterexample from laysa by saying it alone permits omission because it resembles lā; the predicate of other kāna-type verbs is doubly demanded and cannot be deleted.
SAMIN-DURR:2:280/r4.anchor: فالجواب أن هذا مختص بليس، لأنها تشبه لا النافية، و " لا " يجوز حذف خبرها فكذا ما أشبهها

SAMIN-DURR:2:280/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:280/r5.speaker: عبد الله وأبي وعثمان
SAMIN-DURR:2:280/r5.claim: The readings attributed to ʿAbd Allāh, Ubayy, and ʿUthmān use the accusative dhā ʿusratin, supporting the Kufan parse in which the debtor is an implicit subject.
SAMIN-DURR:2:280/r5.anchor: وتقوى الكفيون بقراءة عبد الله وأبي وعثمان: " وإن كان ذا عسرة " أي: وإن كان الغريم ذا عسرة.

SAMIN-DURR:2:280/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:280/r6.speaker: أبو علي
SAMIN-DURR:2:280/r6.claim: Abū ʿAlī supplies an implicit huwa as kāna’s subject, understood as the debtor from the prior discourse about a lender and borrower.
SAMIN-DURR:2:280/r6.anchor: قال أبو علي: " في " كان " اسمها ضميرا تقديره: هو، أي الغريم، يدل على إضماره ما تقدم من الكلام

SAMIN-DURR:2:280/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:280/r7.speaker: الأعمش
SAMIN-DURR:2:280/r7.claim: Al-Aʿmash reads in kāna muʿsiran; al-Dānī reports from Aḥmad ibn Mūsā that this wording is in ʿAbd Allāh’s codex.
SAMIN-DURR:2:280/r7.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش: " وإن كان معسرا " قال الداني عن أحمد بن موسى: " إنها في مصحف عبد الله كذلك.

SAMIN-DURR:2:280/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:280/r8.speaker: الجمهور
SAMIN-DURR:2:280/r8.claim: The majority retain the familiar nominative reading; Makkī says it applies to any insolvent person, whereas accusative dhā would identify a particular debtor or purchaser.
SAMIN-DURR:2:280/r8.anchor: ولكن الجمهور على ترجيح قراءة العامة وتخريجهم القراءة المشهورة. قال مكي: " وإن وقع ذو عسرة، وهو سائغ في كل الناس

SAMIN-DURR:2:280/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:280/r9.speaker: الواحدي
SAMIN-DURR:2:280/r9.claim: Al-Wāḥidī explains that nominative dhū ʿusratin means any insolvent person; the accusative would make the respite specific to the purchaser, though anyone in debt is entitled to it.
SAMIN-DURR:2:280/r9.anchor: وقد أوضح الواحدي هذا فقال: " أي: وإن وقع ذو عسرة، والمعنى على هذا يصح

SAMIN-DURR:2:280/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:280/r10.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:2:280/r10.claim: The Shaykh says the accusative reading or muʿsiran may be specific to usury debtors, while the nominative is general to all debtors.
SAMIN-DURR:2:280/r10.anchor: وقال الشيخ: " من نصب " ذا عسرة " أو قرأ " معسرا "

SAMIN-DURR:2:280/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:280/r11.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:280/r11.claim: The author rejects the suggestion that the ruling is limited to usury debtors: even if the passage arose in that context, its legal scope is not restricted to them.
SAMIN-DURR:2:280/r11.anchor: قلت: وهذا الجواب لا يجدي، لأنه وإن كان السياق كذا فالحكم ليس خاصا بهم.

SAMIN-DURR:2:280#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:280#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:280#2/r1.claim: Fa-naẓiratun answers the condition; it can be a predicate of an omitted subject, a subject with an omitted predicate, or the subject of an implied verb.
SAMIN-DURR:2:280#2/r1.anchor: الفاء جواب الشرط و " نظرة " خبر مبتدأ محذوف، أي: فالأمر أو فالواجب، أو مبتدأ خبره محذوف

SAMIN-DURR:2:280#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:280#2/r2.speaker: العامة
SAMIN-DURR:2:280#2/r2.claim: The common reading is naẓratun, on the pattern of nabqatun.

SAMIN-DURR:2:280#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:280#2/r3.speaker: الحسن ومجاهد وأبو رجاء
SAMIN-DURR:2:280#2/r3.claim: Al-Ḥasan, Mujāhid, and Abū Rajāʾ read naẓratun with a quiescent ʿayn, a Tamīmī dialect pattern.
SAMIN-DURR:2:280#2/r3.anchor: وقرأ الحسن ومجاهد وأبو رجاء: " فنظرة " بتسكين العين، وهي لغة تميمية

SAMIN-DURR:2:280#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:280#2/r4.speaker: عطاء
SAMIN-DURR:2:280#2/r4.claim: ʿAṭāʾ reads nāẓiratan; Abū Isḥāq parses it as a verbal noun, supported by analogous forms in three cited verses.
SAMIN-DURR:2:280#2/r4.anchor: وقرأ عطاء " فناظرة " على فاعلة، وقد خرجها أبو إسحاق على أنها مصدر نحو:

SAMIN-DURR:2:280#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:280#2/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:2:280#2/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī explains nāẓiratan as the right-holder waiting, or as one possessing respite by relational usage; he also transmits an imperative reading meaning to grant the respite.
SAMIN-DURR:2:280#2/r5.anchor: وقال الزمخشري " فناظره أي فصاحب الحق ناظره أي: منتظره، أو صاحب نظرته على طريقة النسب

SAMIN-DURR:2:280#2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:280#2/r6.speaker: عبد الله
SAMIN-DURR:2:280#2/r6.claim: ʿAbd Allāh reads fanāẓirūhu as a plural imperative to grant respite; together with the other reported forms the source counts six readings, though one is standard.
SAMIN-DURR:2:280#2/r6.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله، " فناظروه " أمرا للجماعة بالنظرة، فهذه ست قراءات مشهورها واحد.

SAMIN-DURR:2:280#2/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:280#2/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:280#2/r7.claim: The clause is declarative in form but imperative in meaning, as in the cited verse on mothers nursing; naẓra means waiting, patience, or a respite.
SAMIN-DURR:2:280#2/r7.anchor: وهذه الجملة لفظها خبر ومعناها الأمر، كقوله: والوالدات يرضعن

SAMIN-DURR:2:280#2/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:280#2/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:280#2/r8.anchor:
والعسرة بمعنى العسر.
قوله: { فنظرة } الفاء جواب الشرط و " نظرة " خبر مبتدأ محذوف

SAMIN-DURR:2:280#3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:280#3/r1.speaker: نافع
SAMIN-DURR:2:280#3/r1.claim: Nāfiʿ alone reads maysaratin with a ḍamma on the sīn; the other readers use fatḥa, the more familiar pattern.
SAMIN-DURR:2:280#3/r1.anchor: قرأ نافع وحده: " ميسرة " بضم السين، والباقون بفتحها. والفتح هو المشهور

SAMIN-DURR:2:280#3/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:280#3/r2.speaker: النحاس
SAMIN-DURR:2:280#3/r2.claim: Al-Naḥḥās rejects the ḍamma because he says the pattern mafʿila occurs in only a few words and mufʿal does not occur in ordinary usage.
SAMIN-DURR:2:280#3/r2.anchor: وقد رد النحاس الضم تجرؤا منه، وقال: " لم تأت مفعلة إلا في حروف معدودة ليس هذه منها

SAMIN-DURR:2:280#3/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:280#3/r3.speaker: سيبويه
SAMIN-DURR:2:280#3/r3.claim: Sībawayh says mufʿal does not occur in Arabic; Abū ʿAlī clarifies that he means in singular forms.
SAMIN-DURR:2:280#3/r3.anchor: وقال سيبويه: " ليس في الكلام مفعل " قال أبو علي: " يعني في الآحاد ".

SAMIN-DURR:2:280#3/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:280#3/r4.speaker: الكسائي
SAMIN-DURR:2:280#3/r4.claim: Al-Kisāʾī allows mufʿal among singulars and cites makaraman and maʿūnan; most grammarians instead analyze these apparent examples as plurals.
SAMIN-DURR:2:280#3/r4.anchor: وقال الكسائي: " مفعل " في الآحاد، وأورد منه: مكرما في قول الشاعر

SAMIN-DURR:2:280#3/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:280#3/r5.speaker: عدي
SAMIN-DURR:2:280#3/r5.claim: ʿAdī’s verse supplies maʾlakan as another example offered for the disputed pattern.
SAMIN-DURR:2:280#3/r5.anchor: ومألكا في قول عدي: 1119 أبلغ النعمان عني مألكا

SAMIN-DURR:2:280#3/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:280#3/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:280#3/r6.claim: These apparent singular examples do not refute Sībawayh: most grammarians analyze them as plurals, and Sībawayh disregards rare isolated forms.
SAMIN-DURR:2:280#3/r6.anchor: وهذا لا يرد على سيبويه لوجهين، أحدهما: أن هذا جمع لمكرمة ومعونة ومألكة

SAMIN-DURR:2:280#3/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:280#3/r7.speaker: النحويون
SAMIN-DURR:2:280#3/r7.claim: Grammarians fault Mujāhid and ʿAṭāʾ for reading maysarahu with a genitive pronoun because they assume mufʿal cannot be singular; the author replies that it can be a plural of maysara or a feminine form with its tāʾ omitted in annexation.
SAMIN-DURR:2:280#3/r7.anchor: وإذا تقرر هذا فقد خطأ النحويون مجاهدا وعطاء في قراءتهما: " إلى ميسره " بإضافة " ميسر " مضموم السين إلى ضمير الغريم

SAMIN-DURR:2:280#4/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:280#4/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:280#4/r1.claim: An unnamed poet’s line omits the feminine tāʾ of ʿidda when the word is annexed, supporting the author’s explanation of maysarahu.
SAMIN-DURR:2:280#4/r1.anchor: وأخلفوك عد الأمر الذي وعدوا أي: عدة الأمر

SAMIN-DURR:2:280#4/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:280#4/r2.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:2:280#4/r2.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ suggests maysara comes from maysūra with a deleted wāw; ʿAbd Allāh’s maysūrihi supports this, though it accords only with al-Akhfash’s acceptance of verbal nouns on mafʿūl, unlike Sībawayh.
SAMIN-DURR:2:280#4/r2.anchor: وقد خرجها أبو البقاء على وجه آخر، وهو أن يكون الأصل: " ميسوره " فخفف بحذف الواو

SAMIN-DURR:2:280#4/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:280#4/r3.speaker: عاصم
SAMIN-DURR:2:280#4/r3.claim: ʿĀṣim lightens the ṣād in taṣaddaqū; the other readers double it. Both reflect the underlying tataṣaddaqū, with ʿĀṣim deleting one tāʾ and the others assimilating tāʾ into ṣād.
SAMIN-DURR:2:280#4/r3.anchor: قرأ عاصم بتخفيف الصاد، والباقون بتثقيلها. وأصل القراءتين واحد، إذ الأصل: تتصدقوا

SAMIN-DURR:2:280#4/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:280#4/r4.speaker: عبد الله
SAMIN-DURR:2:280#4/r4.claim: ʿAbd Allāh reads the full underlying form, tataṣaddaqū.
SAMIN-DURR:2:280#4/r4.anchor: وبهذا الأصل قرأ عبد الله: " تتصدقوا ".

SAMIN-DURR:2:280#4/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:280#4/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:280#4/r5.claim: The object of taṣaddaqū is omitted as understood; one interpretation is to grant more time by forgoing the debt, another to remit the principal to the debtor.
SAMIN-DURR:2:280#4/r5.anchor: وحذف مفعول التصدق للعلم به، أي: بالإنظار. وقيل: برأس المال على الغريم.

SAMIN-DURR:2:280#4/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:280#4/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:280#4/r6.claim: The answer to in kuntum taʿlamūn is omitted, while an taṣaddaqū is a verbal-noun clause serving as subject of khayrun lakum.
SAMIN-DURR:2:280#4/r6.anchor: و { إن كنتم تعلمون } جوابه محذوف. و " أن تصدقوا " بتأويل مصدر مبتدأ، و " خير لكم " خبره

RAZI-FULL:v7p88/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p88/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p88/r3.claim: Grammarians use kāna either as a complete verb meaning occurred or existed, with no predicate, or as a defective verb that needs a predicate.
RAZI-FULL:v7p88/r3.anchor: أن تكون بمنزلة حدث ووقع ، وذلك في قوله : قد كان الأمر ، أي وجد

RAZI-FULL:v7p88/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p88/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p88/r4.claim: In its defective use, kāna sheds the separate event meaning and marks time, so it requires a predicate, as in ‘Zayd was going.’
RAZI-FULL:v7p88/r4.anchor: أن يخلع منه معنى الحدث ، فتبقى الكلمة مجردة للزمان ، وحينئذ يحتاج إلى الخبر

RAZI-FULL:v7p88/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p88/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p88/r5.claim: In Khwarazm, Razi challenged leading litterateurs: if kāna is a verb it must be complete, while if incomplete it would have to be a particle, contrary to their view.
RAZI-FULL:v7p88/r5.anchor: إنكم تقولون إن { كان } إذا كانت ناقصة إنها تكون فعلا وهذا محال

RAZI-FULL:v7p88/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p88/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p88/r6.claim: Razi says kāna means an event or occurrence in both uses: a complete verb marks an entity’s occurrence, while a defective one marks the occurrence of a subject’s being described by a predicate.
RAZI-FULL:v7p88/r6.anchor: المفهوم من { كان } في الموضعين هو الحدوث والوقوع

RAZI-FULL:v7p89/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p89/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p89/r1.claim: Kāna can mean ‘became’; an anonymous poetic line about birds and their eggs illustrates this sense.
RAZI-FULL:v7p89/r1.anchor: بتيهاء قفر والمطي كأنها قطا الحزن قد كانت فراخا بيوضها

RAZI-FULL:v7p89/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p89/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p89/r2.claim: Razi explains ‘became’ as a new occurrence in which a subject acquires a description it did not previously have.
RAZI-FULL:v7p89/r2.anchor: حدث موصوفية الذات بهذه الصفة بعد أنها ما كانت موصوفة بذلك

RAZI-FULL:v7p89/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p89/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p89/r3.claim: Grammarians also treat kāna as redundant, citing an anonymous line about fine horses.
RAZI-FULL:v7p89/r3.anchor: سراة بني أبي بكر تسامى على كان المسومة الجياد

RAZI-FULL:v7p89/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p89/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p89/r4.claim: Razi reads kāna here as a complete verb meaning ‘occurred’: whenever anyone is in hardship, that person receives respite; reading it as ‘if the buyer is insolvent’ would wrongly narrow the rule.
RAZI-FULL:v7p89/r4.anchor: أنها بمعنى وقع وحدث ، والمعنى : وإن وجد ذو عسرة

RAZI-FULL:v7p89/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p89/r5.speaker: عثمان
RAZI-FULL:v7p89/r5.claim: An alternative parses kāna as defective with an omitted predicate, ‘a debtor to you’; Uthman’s accusative reading and another reported reading make the debtor explicit.
RAZI-FULL:v7p89/r5.anchor: وقرأ عثمان { ذا * عسرة } والتقدير : إن كان الغريم ذا عسرة

RAZI-FULL:v7p89/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p89/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p89/r6.claim: Al-ʿUsra is inability to find available money, the condition in which money is hard to obtain.
RAZI-FULL:v7p89/r6.anchor: العسرة اسم من الأعسار ، وهو تعذر الموجود من المال

RAZI-FULL:v7p89/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p89/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p89/r7.claim: The clause omits its subject or predicate: the implied meaning is that the ruling, command, or person you deal with is respite.
RAZI-FULL:v7p89/r7.anchor: في الآية حذف ، والتقدير : فالحكم أو فالأمر نظرة

RAZI-FULL:v7p89/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p89/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p89/r8.claim: Naẓira means delay or granting respite, as in the request to be kept waiting until the appointed time.
RAZI-FULL:v7p89/r8.anchor: نظرة أي تأخير ، والنظرة الاسم من الأنظار ، وهو الإمهال

RAZI-FULL:v7p89#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p89#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p89#2/r1.claim: A reading has naẓira with a quiescent ẓāʾ; ʿAṭāʾ reads nāẓirahu, meaning the creditor waits or is the holder of the respite.
RAZI-FULL:v7p89#2/r1.anchor: وقرأ عطاء { * فناظره } أي فصاحب الحق أي منتظره

RAZI-FULL:v7p89#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p89#2/r2.speaker: عطاء
RAZI-FULL:v7p89#2/r2.claim: A further reading attributed to ʿAṭāʾ is an imperative: grant the debtor respite until ease.
RAZI-FULL:v7p89#2/r2.anchor: وعنه فناظره على الأمر أي فسامحه بالنظرة إلى الميسرة

RAZI-FULL:v7p89#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p89#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p89#2/r3.claim: Maysara derives from ease and wealth, the opposite of hardship; maysara, yusr, and maysūr all mean wealth.
RAZI-FULL:v7p89#2/r3.anchor: الميسرة مفعلة من اليسر واليسار ، الذي هو ضد الأعسار

RAZI-FULL:v7p89#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p89#2/r4.speaker: نافع
RAZI-FULL:v7p89#2/r4.claim: Nāfiʿ reads maysara with a ḍamma on the sīn; the other readers use a fatḥa, the more common of the two dialect forms.
RAZI-FULL:v7p89#2/r4.anchor: قرأ نافع { إلى ميسرة } بضم السين والباقون بفتحها

RAZI-FULL:v7p89#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p89#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس وشريح والضحاك والسدي وإبراهيم
RAZI-FULL:v7p89#2/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Shurayḥ, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, al-Suddī, and Ibrāhīm hold that the respite rule applies to usurious debts.
RAZI-FULL:v7p89#2/r5.anchor: فقال ابن عباس وشريح والضحاك والسدي وإبراهيم : الآية في الربا

RAZI-FULL:v7p89#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p89#2/r6.speaker: شريح
RAZI-FULL:v7p89#2/r6.claim: Shurayḥ reportedly ordered a debtor jailed despite a claim of insolvency, explaining that the respite rule concerns usury and citing the duty to return trusts.
RAZI-FULL:v7p89#2/r6.anchor: فقال شريح : إنما ذلك في الربا ، والله تعالى قال في كتابه

RAZI-FULL:v7p89#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p89#2/r7.speaker: مفسرون
RAZI-FULL:v7p89#2/r7.claim: Commentators report that four brothers who had dealt in usury agreed to take only their principal after the threat of war, but Banu al-Mughira could not pay until the harvest and were refused delay; then this verse was revealed.
RAZI-FULL:v7p89#2/r7.anchor: فشكا بنو المغيرة العسرة ، وقالوا : أخرونا إلى أن تدرك الغلات ، فأبوا أن يؤخروهم

RAZI-FULL:v7p89#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p89#2/r8.speaker: مجاهد وجماعة من المفسرين
RAZI-FULL:v7p89#2/r8.claim: Mujāhid and a group of commentators apply the rule to all debts, arguing that the wording does not restrict hardship to the purchaser.
RAZI-FULL:v7p89#2/r8.anchor: القول الثاني : وهو قول مجاهد وجماعة من المفسرين : إنها عامة في كل دين

RAZI-FULL:v7p89#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p89#2/r9.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v7p89#2/r9.claim: The Qadi says the context makes the usury-specific reading stronger because the preceding passage addresses usury and its threat of war.
RAZI-FULL:v7p89#2/r9.anchor: والقول الأول أرجح ، لأنه تعالى قال في الآية المتقدمة

RAZI-FULL:v7p89#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p89#2/r10.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v7p89#2/r10.claim: The Qadi extends the duty to other debts by the shared reason that one unable to pay cannot be charged with payment; Razi says this is the majority jurists’ view, including Abu Hanifa, Malik, and al-Shafiʿi.
RAZI-FULL:v7p89#2/r10.anchor: ثبت وجوبه في سائر الصور ضرورة الاشتراك في المعنى ، وهو أن العاجز عن أداء المال لا يجوز تكليفه به

RAZI-FULL:v7p90/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p90/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p90/r1.claim: A debtor is insolvent only if the estate has neither property available to pay the debt nor assets that could be sold to cover it.
RAZI-FULL:v7p90/r1.anchor: الإعسار هو أن لا يجد في ملكه ما يؤديه بعينه ، ولا يكون له ما لو باعه

RAZI-FULL:v7p90/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p90/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p90/r2.claim: A debtor who owns a house or clothes is not insolvent if they can be sold to pay the debt, but may keep daily food and necessary clothes for prayer and protection from weather.
RAZI-FULL:v7p90/r2.anchor: من وحد دارا وثيابا لا يعد في ذوي العسرة ، إذا ما أمكنه بيعها

RAZI-FULL:v7p90/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p90/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p90/r3.claim: Jurists disagree whether an able-bodied insolvent debtor must hire out his labor to the creditor or another person to pay the debt.
RAZI-FULL:v7p90/r3.anchor: واختلفوا إذا كان قويا هل يلزمه أن يؤاجر نفسه من صاحب الدين أو غيره

RAZI-FULL:v7p90/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p90/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p90/r4.claim: Jurists also disagree whether an insolvent debtor must accept another person’s offer to pay the debt on his behalf.
RAZI-FULL:v7p90/r4.anchor: إذا كان معسرا ، وقد بذل غيره ما يؤديه ، هل يلزمه القبول والأداء أو لا يلزمه ذلك

RAZI-FULL:v7p90/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p90/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p90/r5.claim: A debtor with goods that have become unsalable must sell them at a loss if necessary and apply the proceeds to the debt.
RAZI-FULL:v7p90/r5.anchor: فأما من له بضاعة كسدت عليه ، فواجب عليه أن يبيعها بالنقصان إن لم يكن إلا ذلك

RAZI-FULL:v7p90/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p90/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p90/r6.claim: Knowingly imprisoning a proven insolvent debtor or demanding payment is wrongful; the creditor must wait until the debtor becomes solvent.
RAZI-FULL:v7p90/r6.anchor: إذا علم الإنسان أن غريمه معسر جرم عليه حبسه ، وأن يطالبه بما له عليه

RAZI-FULL:v7p90/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p90/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p90/r7.claim: If the creditor has reason to doubt the insolvency claim, detention is allowed until the debtor’s status becomes clear.
RAZI-FULL:v7p90/r7.anchor: فأما إن كانت له ريبة في إعساره فيجوز له أن يحبسه إلى وقت ظهور الإعسار

RAZI-FULL:v7p90/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p90/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p90/r8.claim: For a debt arising from sale or loan, a debtor disputing insolvency must produce two upright witnesses that the received consideration was lost.
RAZI-FULL:v7p90/r8.anchor: وفي القسم الأول لا بد من إقامة شاهدين عدلين على أن ذلك العوض قد هلك

RAZI-FULL:v7p90/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p90/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p90/r9.claim: For a debt without consideration, such as damages, dowry, or guarantee, the debtor’s word is accepted and creditors must prove otherwise because poverty is the presumption.
RAZI-FULL:v7p90/r9.anchor: كان القول قوله وعلى الغرماء البينة لأن الأصل هو الفقر

RAZI-FULL:v7p90/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p90/r10.speaker: عاصم
RAZI-FULL:v7p90/r10.claim: ʿĀṣim reads tasaddaqu with a light ṣād; the other readers geminate it, reflecting deletion or assimilation of one of the original two tāʾs.
RAZI-FULL:v7p90/r10.anchor: قرأ عاصم { تصدقوا } بتخفيف الصاد والباقون بتشديدها

RAZI-FULL:v7p90/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p90/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p90/r11.claim: One interpretation is that creditors forgive some or all of the debt owed by the insolvent; the omitted object is clear from the preceding mention of the debtor and principal.
RAZI-FULL:v7p90/r11.anchor: وأن تصدقوا على المعسر بما عليه من الدين إذ لا يصح التصدق به على غيره

RAZI-FULL:v7p90/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p90/r12.speaker: النبي
RAZI-FULL:v7p90/r12.claim: A Prophetic report says that whoever delays a Muslim’s due debt receives the reward of charity for each day of delay.
RAZI-FULL:v7p90/r12.anchor: لقوله عليه السلام ( لا يحل دين رجل مسلم فيؤخره إلا كان له بكل يوم صدقة )

RAZI-FULL:v7p90/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p90/r13.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p90/r13.claim: The second interpretation takes charity to mean granting more time, but Razi rejects it because respite is already obligatory and ‘better for you’ fits a recommended act.
RAZI-FULL:v7p90/r13.anchor: هذا القول ضعيف ، لأن الإنظار ثبت وجوبه بالآية الأولى

RAZI-FULL:v7p91/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p91/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p91/r1.claim: The good promised by charity is honorable praise in this world and abundant reward in the hereafter.
RAZI-FULL:v7p91/r1.anchor: المراد بالخير حصول الثناء الجميل في الدنيا والثواب الجزيل في الآخرة

RAZI-FULL:v7p91/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p91/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p91/r2.claim: One reading of ‘if you know’ makes acting on the knowledge a condition, which serves as a severe warning to those who disobey.
RAZI-FULL:v7p91/r2.anchor: فجعل العمل من لوازم العلم ، وفيه تهديد شديد على العصاة

RAZI-FULL:v7p91/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p91/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p91/r3.claim: A second reading means if you know that charity is better than granting respite and collecting the debt.
RAZI-FULL:v7p91/r3.anchor: إن كنتم تعلمون فضل التصدق على الإنظار والقبض

RAZI-FULL:v7p91/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p91/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p91/r4.claim: A third reading means if you know that what your Lord commands is more beneficial for you.
RAZI-FULL:v7p91/r4.anchor: إن كنتم تعلمون أن ما يأمركم به ربكم أصلح لكم

STUDYQURAN:2:275/r38.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:275/r38.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:275/r38.claim: Islamic loans, unlike investments, were ideally charitable because money’s time factor matters and credit sales or leases could serve non-charitable investment and fundraising.
STUDYQURAN:2:275/r38.anchor: In the Islamic tradition, loans (as opposed to investments) were ideally charitable in nature, owing to the time factor in giving and taking money

STUDYQURAN:2:275/r39.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:275/r39.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:275/r39.claim: The passage invites creditors to turn ribā-laden loans into charity when debtors are in dire financial difficulty.
STUDYQURAN:2:275/r39.anchor: in the case of a debtor in dire financial circumstances

STUDYQURAN:2:275/r40.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:275/r40.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:275/r40.claim: A hadith credits a lender with one act of charity for each day of delay granted to someone in difficulty.
STUDYQURAN:2:275/r40.anchor: A ḥadīth states, “Whosoever grants a delay to one in difficult circumstances shall be credited an act of charity for each day of it.”

STUDYQURAN:2:275/r41.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:275/r41.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:275/r41.claim: The verse encourages respite until the debtor has ease but does not require it or remove the lender’s claim to principal.
STUDYQURAN:2:275/r41.anchor: This does not negate the claim of a lender to the original principal, since the verse encourages a respite until there is ease, but does not require it (Q).

TAB-FULL:v5p56/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p56/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p56/r1.claim: The verse commands creditors to defer collection of principal from an insolvent debtor until the debtor becomes able to pay.
TAB-FULL:v5p56/r1.anchor: ومعنى الكلام: وإن كان من غرمائكم ذو عسرة، فعليكم أن تنظروه حتى يوسر بما ليس لكم

TAB-FULL:v5p56/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p56/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p56/r2.claim: ذو عسرة is nominative as the subject of kāna, with its predicate omitted; Arabic can leave a predicate understood for an indefinite noun.
TAB-FULL:v5p56/r2.anchor: وقوله: {ذو عسرة} [البقرة: 280] مرفوع بكان، فالخبر متروك، وهو ما ذكرنا

TAB-FULL:v5p56/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p56/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p56/r3.claim: Alternatively, kāna here can be a complete verb needing no predicate, meaning that an insolvent debtor is found among the creditors' debtors.
TAB-FULL:v5p56/r3.anchor: ولو وجهت كان في هذا الموضع إلى أنها بمعنى الفعل المكتفي بنفسه التام، لكان وجها صحيحا

TAB-FULL:v5p56/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p56/r4.speaker: أبي بن كعب
TAB-FULL:v5p56/r4.claim: A reading attributed to Ubayy has ذا عسرة, which is grammatically possible, but al-Ṭabarī rejects it as a recitation because it conflicts with the written muṣḥafs.
TAB-FULL:v5p56/r4.anchor: وذلك وإن كان في العربية جائزا فغير جائزة القراءة به عندنا لخلافه خطوط مصاحف المسلمين

TAB-FULL:v5p56/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p56/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p56/r5.claim: فنظرة means that creditors are obliged to grant the debtor time until able to pay.
TAB-FULL:v5p56/r5.anchor: فإنه يعني: فعليكم أن تنظروه إلى ميسرة

TAB-FULL:v5p56/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p56/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p56/r6.claim: Maysara is formed from yusr on the pattern of marḥama and mashʾama.
TAB-FULL:v5p56/r6.anchor: والميسرة: المفعلة من اليسر، مثل المرحمة والمشأمة

TAB-FULL:v5p56/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p56/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v5p56/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the verse was revealed concerning usury.
TAB-FULL:v5p56/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس، في قوله: {وإن كان ذو عسرة فنظرة إلى ميسرة} [البقرة: 280] قال: «نزلت في الربا»

TAB-FULL:v5p56/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p56/r8.speaker: شريح
TAB-FULL:v5p56/r8.claim: In a case about an allegedly insolvent debtor, Shurayḥ says this deferral applies to usury; ordinary trusts must still be returned as 4:58 commands.
TAB-FULL:v5p56/r8.anchor: فقال شريح: " إنما ذلك في الربا، وإن الله قال في كتابه: {إن الله يأمركم أن تؤدوا الأمانات إلى أهلها وإذا حكمتم بين الناس أن تحكموا بالعدل} [النساء: 58]

TAB-FULL:v5p59/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p59/r1.speaker: إبراهيم
TAB-FULL:v5p59/r1.claim: Ibrāhīm says the deferral instruction concerns usury.
TAB-FULL:v5p59/r1.anchor: عن إبراهيم، في قوله: {وإن كان ذو عسرة فنظرة إلى ميسرة} [البقرة: 280] قال: «ذلك في الربا»

TAB-FULL:v5p59/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p59/r2.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v5p59/r2.claim: Al-Ḥasan recounts that al-Rabīʿ ibn Khuthaym would tell a creditor to pay if solvent and defer if insolvent.
TAB-FULL:v5p59/r2.anchor: عن الحسن: أن الربيع بن خثيم، كان له على رجل حق، فكان يأتيه ويقوم على بابه ويقول

TAB-FULL:v5p59/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p59/r3.speaker: شريح
TAB-FULL:v5p59/r3.claim: Shurayḥ again limits the verse to usury and says God would not command repayment of trusts and then punish people for obeying that command.
TAB-FULL:v5p59/r3.anchor: فقال شريح: " إن الربا كان في هذا الحي من الأنصار، فأنزل الله عز وجل: {وإن كان ذو عسرة فنظرة إلى ميسرة} [البقرة: 280] وقال الله عز وجل: {إن الله يأمركم أن تؤدوا الأمانات إلى أهلها}

TAB-FULL:v5p59/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p59/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v5p59/r4.claim: Qatāda specifies that the creditor must defer collection of the principal until the debtor is able.
TAB-FULL:v5p59/r4.anchor: عن قتادة، في قوله: {وإن كان ذو عسرة فنظرة إلى ميسرة} [البقرة: 280] قال: «فنظرة إلى ميسرة برأس ماله»

TAB-FULL:v5p59/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p59/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v5p59/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the instruction to defer concerns usury, not trusts, which must be repaid to their owners.
TAB-FULL:v5p59/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس: {وإن كان ذو عسرة فنظرة إلى ميسرة} [البقرة: 280] «إنما أمر في الربا أن ينظر المعسر، وليست النظرة في الأمانة، ولكن يؤدي الأمانة إلى أهلها»

TAB-FULL:v5p59/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p59/r6.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v5p59/r6.claim: Al-Suddī glosses deferral as waiting for the debtor to become wealthy enough to repay the principal.
TAB-FULL:v5p59/r6.anchor: عن السدي: {وإن كان ذو عسرة فنظرة} [البقرة: 280] «برأس المال» ، {إلى ميسرة} [البقرة: 280] يقول: «إلى غنى»

TAB-FULL:v5p61/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p61/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v5p61/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses the insolvent person as the debtor who is being pursued for payment.
TAB-FULL:v5p61/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس: {وإن كان ذو عسرة فنظرة إلى ميسرة} [البقرة: 280] «يعني المطلوب»

TAB-FULL:v5p61/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p61/r2.speaker: أبو جعفر
TAB-FULL:v5p61/r2.claim: Abū Jaʿfar interprets the term maysara as death; a second route reports the same gloss from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī.
TAB-FULL:v5p61/r2.anchor: عن أبي جعفر، في قوله: {وإن كان ذو عسرة فنظرة إلى ميسرة} [البقرة: 280] قال: «الموت»

TAB-FULL:v5p61/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p61/r3.speaker: إبراهيم
TAB-FULL:v5p61/r3.claim: Ibrāhīm reiterates that the verse concerns usury.
TAB-FULL:v5p61/r3.anchor: عن إبراهيم: {وإن كان ذو عسرة فنظرة إلى ميسرة} [البقرة: 280] قال: «هذا في الربا»

TAB-FULL:v5p61/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p61/r4.speaker: إبراهيم
TAB-FULL:v5p61/r4.claim: On a man who marries until maysara, Ibrāhīm says the term means until death or separation.
TAB-FULL:v5p61/r4.anchor: عن إبراهيم، في الرجل يتزوج إلى الميسرة، قال: «إلى الموت أو إلى فرقة»

TAB-FULL:v5p61/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p61/r5.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v5p61/r5.claim: Mujāhid says creditors should defer a debt without increasing it; people had been adding to debts and extending them when debtors could not pay at maturity.
TAB-FULL:v5p61/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد: { فنظرة إلى ميسرة} [البقرة: 280] قال: «يؤخره ولا يزد عليه، وكان إذا حل دين أحدهم فلم يجد ما يعطيه زاد عليه وأخره»

TAB-FULL:v5p61/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p61/r6.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v5p61/r6.claim: Another group says the rule covers every debt owed to a creditor by an insolvent person, whether the debt arose lawfully or through usury.
TAB-FULL:v5p61/r6.anchor: وقال آخرون: هذه الآية عامة في كل من كان له قبل رجل معسر حق من أي وجهة كان ذلك الحق من دين حلال أو ربا

TAB-FULL:v5p61/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p61/r7.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v5p61/r7.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says a Muslim creditor who knows a fellow Muslim is insolvent may neither imprison nor press him for payment until God makes him solvent.
TAB-FULL:v5p61/r7.anchor: فلا يحل لمسلم له دين على أخيه يعلم منه عسرة أن يسجنه ولا يطلبه حتى ييسره الله عليه

TAB-FULL:v5p61#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p61#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v5p61#2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that the verse was revealed concerning debt.
TAB-FULL:v5p61#2/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد، عن ابن عباس: {وإن كان ذو عسرة فنظرة إلى ميسرة} [البقرة: 280] قال ": نزلت في الدين "

TAB-FULL:v5p61#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p61#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p61#2/r2.claim: Al-Ṭabarī says the immediate context is converts owed pre-Islamic usury: interest is void, the principal remains, and insolvent debtors receive time until they can pay it.
TAB-FULL:v5p61#2/r2.anchor: فأمر الله بوضع ما بقي من الربا بعد ما أسلموا، وبقبض رءوس أموالهم، ممن كان منهم من غرمائهم موسرا، وإنظار من كان منهم معسرا برءوس أموالهم إلى ميسرتهم

TAB-FULL:v5p61#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p61#2/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p61#2/r3.claim: Although revealed about usury, the same ruling obliges deferral for anyone unable to pay a due debt, including an ordinary lawful debt.
TAB-FULL:v5p61#2/r3.anchor: فإن الحكم الذي حكم الله به من إنظاره المعسر برأس مال المربي بعد بطول الربا عنه حكم واجب لكل من كان عليه دين لرجل قد حل عليه، وهو بقضائه معسر في أنه منظر إلى ميسرته

TAB-FULL:v5p61#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p61#2/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p61#2/r4.claim: A debt is owed from debtor property rather than the debtor person; if no property is available, the creditor cannot jail or sell the debtor, since the debtor is not withholding a payable asset.
TAB-FULL:v5p61#2/r4.anchor: فإذا عدم ماله، فلا سبيل له على رقبته بحبس ولا بيع، وذلك أن مال رب الدين لن يخلو من أحد وجوه ثلاثة

TAB-FULL:v5p63/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p63/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p63/r1.claim: Al-Tabari says those who understand know the merit and reward of charity that removes an insolvent debtor's obligation.
TAB-FULL:v5p63/r1.anchor: من الثواب لمن وضع عن غريمه المعسر دينه

TAB-FULL:v5p63/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p63/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v5p63/r3.claim: One reported interpretation takes the charity as giving up principal owed by both wealthy and poor debtors.
TAB-FULL:v5p63/r3.anchor: يقول وإن تصدقوا بأصل المال، خير لكم

TAB-FULL:v5p63/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p63/r4.speaker: إبراهيم
TAB-FULL:v5p63/r4.claim: Ibrahim interprets the charity as forgiving the principal of the debt.
TAB-FULL:v5p63/r4.anchor: عن مغيرة، عن إبراهيم: {وأن تصدقوا خير لكم} [البقرة: 280] قال: «من رءوس أموالكم»

TAB-FULL:v5p63/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p63/r5.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v5p63/r5.claim: The charity means forgiving principal to the poor; al-Abbas did so.
